title: Asesmen Visual Kondisi Fisik Permukiman dan Identifikasi Kebutuhan Mitigasi Bencana pada Kawasan Hunian Baru Masyarakat Adat Pascakebakaran
abstractText: Pembangunan kembali permukiman pascabencana memerlukan perhatian terhadap kondisi fisik lahan, sistem konstruksi, infrastruktur dasar, dan upaya pengurangan risiko bencana pada kawasan hunian baru. Pada masyarakat adat, kebutuhan tersebut perlu dipertimbangkan bersama keberlanjutan karakter permukiman tradisional. Artikel ini bertujuan mengidentifikasi kondisi fisik dan kebutuhan mitigasi bencana pada kawasan permukiman baru masyarakat adat Kasepuhan Ciptamulya–Mulyaraksa, Kabupaten Sukabumi, Jawa Barat, setelah kebakaran permukiman. Kegiatan dilaksanakan melalui asesmen visual pendahuluan pada Oktober 2026 menggunakan observasi lapangan, dokumentasi kondisi kawasan, serta wawancara dengan pemimpin adat. Aspek yang diamati meliputi penataan lahan, material bangunan yang tampak, infrastruktur dasar, akses kawasan, dan kondisi lingkungan pembangunan. Hasil pengamatan menunjukkan adanya kegiatan pengolahan lahan, penggunaan alat berat, pembangunan dengan kombinasi unsur konstruksi tradisional dan material modern, serta penyediaan sejumlah fasilitas dasar. Keterangan lapangan juga menunjukkan kebutuhan jaringan penyaluran air menuju permukiman baru. Pengamatan terhadap perubahan bentuk lahan mengidentifikasi perlunya perhatian teknis terhadap pengelolaan air permukaan dan stabilitas lereng, tetapi belum memungkinkan penetapan tingkat bahaya longsor. Hasil kegiatan berupa inventarisasi awal kondisi fisik, aspek yang memerlukan pemeriksaan teknis, dan rekomendasi kebutuhan mitigasi untuk mendukung perencanaan permukiman yang lebih aman. Asesmen ini tidak menggantikan penyelidikan tanah, pengujian material, atau pemeriksaan kelaikan struktur bangunan.

title: Asesmen Pemetaan Jaringan Distribusi Bantuan dan Kebutuhan Logistik Masyarakat Adat Pascabencana Kebakaran Permukiman di Kasepuhan Ciptamulya, Kabupaten Sukabumi
abstractText: Pemulihan masyarakat pascabencana memerlukan pengelolaan bantuan dan sumber daya logistik yang melibatkan berbagai aktor, baik pemerintah maupun jaringan sosial masyarakat. Pada komunitas adat, mekanisme distribusi bantuan juga dapat berkaitan dengan kepemimpinan lokal, hubungan kekerabatan, dan praktik gotong royong. Artikel ini bertujuan memetakan jaringan distribusi bantuan serta mengidentifikasi kebutuhan logistik masyarakat adat Kasepuhan Ciptamulya, Kabupaten Sukabumi, setelah kebakaran permukiman. Kegiatan dilaksanakan melalui asesmen lapangan awal pada Oktober 2026 dengan metode observasi, wawancara dengan pemimpin adat, dan dokumentasi kondisi permukiman lama serta pembangunan kawasan baru. Hasil asesmen mengidentifikasi keterlibatan pemerintah, jaringan keluarga besar atau incu putu, pemimpin adat, dan relawan dalam mendukung pemulihan komunitas. Bantuan yang teridentifikasi mencakup makanan, kebutuhan pokok, dukungan tenaga, peralatan, dan material pembangunan. Pemimpin adat memiliki peran dalam penerimaan serta penyaluran sebagian bantuan kepada warga. Pada tahap pembangunan permukiman baru, kebutuhan logistik bergeser menuju penyediaan sarana pendukung hunian dan infrastruktur dasar, termasuk jaringan penyaluran air. Pemetaan menunjukkan pentingnya hubungan antara jaringan bantuan eksternal dan kapasitas pengorganisasian lokal dalam proses pemulihan. Kegiatan ini menghasilkan identifikasi awal aktor, bentuk dukungan, dan kebutuhan logistik yang dapat digunakan sebagai informasi pendahuluan dalam perencanaan pengabdian kepada masyarakat. Hasil asesmen belum mencakup evaluasi efektivitas distribusi maupun pemeriksaan menyeluruh atas volume bantuan.

title: இநதய அறவ மரபல கலததன சரபததனம: வத–பரண இலககயஙகளன மனத–தவ கலக கணககட, வனயல அறவ மறறம நவன சரபயல கலக கரததகளன பனமக ஆயவ: A Multifaceted Study of Human–Divine Time Calculation in Vedic–Puranic Literature, Astronomical Knowledge, and Modern Concepts of Relativistic Time
abstractText: This paper presents a comparative analysis between the conceptual framework of time in the Indian Vedic–Puranic tradition and the concept of time dilation in Albert Einstein’s Theory of Relativity, examining five structural elements: the nature of time, measurement systems, observer-dependent perception, astronomical cycles, and immense cosmic time scales. Crucially, the study maintains epistemological integrity by rejecting the unscientific claim that ancient texts foresaw modern physics; instead, it emphasizes that while both systems developed from completely distinct physical, mathematical, and methodological foundations, they share intriguing structural parallels in recognizing time as relative—evidenced by the observer-dependent hierarchy of human, divine, and cosmic time in Puranas alongside frame-dependent relative time in modern physics.

title: ஆறம வறறமயன கரகத தகதயம மழயயல மரணபடகளம: The Sixth Case in Tamil: Its Kāraka Status and Linguistic Contradictions — A Critical Study
abstractText: Traditional Tamil grammar recognises eight cases. The second to the seventh cases relate a noun to the verb and so express kāraka (case) relations. The sixth case alone relates one noun to another, expressing possession (kizhamai), and has no direct link to the verb. This paper asks whether such a category belongs in the case system at all. The study draws on Tolkāppiyam and Naṉṉūl, Pāṇini's kāraka theory, modern case theory and grammaticalization theory. Five syntactic tests — head type, recursion, clitic attachment, word-order freedom and nominalisation — show the sixth case consistently behaving unlike the other cases. Its main modern marker, uṭaiya, is a relative participle derived from the verb root uṭai 'possess', which points to an adjectival origin. Comparative evidence from Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Tulu shows the same adnominal pattern across the Dravidian family. The paper also weighs the debate over the parallel between the Tamil eight-case scheme and the Sanskrit vibhakti system, noting that Pāṇini himself does not treat the genitive as a kāraka. It concludes that the Tamil sixth case is better analysed as a nominal (adnominal) modifier than as a kāraka case.

title: Comparison of the Effectiveness of Compassion-Focused Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and Schema-Integrated Acceptance and Commitment Therapy on Body Image and Sexual Relationship Quality in Women with Breast Cancer in Hamadan
abstractText: Purpose: This study aimed to compare the effectiveness of Compassion-Focused Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and Schema-Integrated Acceptance and Commitment Therapy on body image and sexual relationship quality in women with breast cancer in Hamadan. Methods and Materials: This applied quasi-experimental study employed a pretest–posttest design with a two-month follow-up, two experimental groups, and one active control group. The statistical population consisted of women with breast cancer attending the Health Donors Association of Hamadan Province during 2025–2026. Sixty eligible women were selected through convenience sampling and randomly assigned to three groups of 20 participants. Following attrition, the final sample comprised 50 women, including 17 in the Compassion-Focused Acceptance and Commitment Therapy group, 16 in the Schema-Integrated Acceptance and Commitment Therapy group, and 17 in the control group. The experimental groups received 10 weekly 90-minute group sessions of their respective interventions, while the control group received five weekly 60-minute health and life-skills education sessions. Data were collected using the Objectified Body Consciousness Scale and the Sexual Quality of Life–Female Questionnaire. Data were analyzed in SPSS version 26 using multivariate and univariate analyses of covariance and Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Findings: Multivariate analysis showed a significant overall effect of treatment condition on the combined dependent variables, Pillai’s Trace = 0.592, F(4, 90) = 9.468, p < 0.001, partial η² = 0.296. Significant group effects were found for body image, F(2, 45) = 20.691, p < 0.001, partial η² = 0.482, and sexual relationship quality, F(2, 45) = 16.250, p < 0.001, partial η² = 0.419. Bonferroni comparisons indicated that both interventions were significantly more effective than the control condition on both outcomes. Compassion-Focused Acceptance and Commitment Therapy was also significantly more effective than Schema-Integrated Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for body image, p = 0.006, and sexual relationship quality, p = 0.031. Conclusion: Both interventions were effective in improving body image and sexual relationship quality among women with breast cancer, although Compassion-Focused Acceptance and Commitment Therapy demonstrated greater effectiveness and may therefore be particularly useful in psycho-oncological rehabilitation following breast cancer treatment.

title: Perancangan dan Implementasi Aplikasi Web Bank Sampah Taman Nuri dengan Pendekatan Rapid Application Development (RAD)
abstractText: Pencatatan manual pada Bank Sampah Taman Nuri, Kabupaten Tangerang, menyebabkan administrasi nasabah, transaksi, dan pelaporan belum terintegrasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang dan mengimplementasikan aplikasi web yang menghubungkan pengelolaan nasabah, penyetoran sampah, penjualan kepada pengepul, penarikan sistem biaya operasional, dan laporan. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui wawancara dengan penanggung jawab bank sampah, observasi proses bisnis, serta analisis dokumen administrasi. Pengembangan menggunakan pendekatan Rapid Application Development (RAD) dengan pemodelan use case, class, dan activity diagram serta rancangan sequence sebagai pelengkap analisis. Hasil yang terdokumentasi berupa lima kelompok modul, yaitu konfigurasi, master data, nasabah, transaksi, dan laporan. Alur penarikan sistem memisahkan pengajuan nasabah dari persetujuan bendahara, sedangkan laporan mencakup laba rugi, penjualan, penyetoran, dan sistem rekening. Telaah keterlacakan menunjukkan keterhubungan konseptual antara kebutuhan operasional dan modul aplikasi. Namun, dokumentasi penelitian belum menyediakan hasil pengujian fungsional terstruktur, pengukuran waktu layanan, atau evaluasi pengguna. Oleh karena itu, kontribusi penelitian dibatasi pada rancangan dan implementasi integrasi administrasi; peningkatan efisiensi, akurasi, dan partisipasi masih memerlukan pembuktian empiris.

title: Pengaruh Fitur Penawaran Digital terhadap Keputusan Pembelian pada Platform Shopee
abstractText: Penelitian ini menganalisis pengaruh fitur penawaran digital terhadap keputusan pembelian pengguna Shopee pada mahasiswa Program Studi Manajemen Bisnis Politeknik Negeri Medan. Pendekatan yang digunakan adalah kuantitatif dengan desain survei. Dari populasi 482 mahasiswa, sebanyak 82 responden dipilih secara purposive dengan kriteria pernah berbelanja di Shopee dan pernah melihat fitur penawaran digital. Data diperoleh melalui kuesioner skala Likert 1–5 dan dianalisis menggunakan uji validitas, reliabilitas, normalitas, heteroskedastisitas, regresi linear sederhana, uji t, dan koefisien determinasi. Seluruh item dinyatakan valid, sedangkan reliabilitas konstruk menunjukkan Cronbach’s Alpha 0,940 untuk penawaran digital dan 0,861 untuk keputusan pembelian. Model memenuhi asumsi normalitas dan tidak menunjukkan gejala heteroskedastisitas. Persamaan regresi yang diperoleh adalah Y = 34,551 + 0,293X. Nilai t hitung 10,739 dengan signifikansi 0,000 menunjukkan bahwa penawaran digital berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Nilai R² sebesar 0,590 menunjukkan bahwa penawaran digital menjelaskan 59% variasi keputusan pembelian. Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa kemudahan, relevansi, kejelasan, dan ketepatan waktu penawaran digital dapat memperkuat keyakinan serta mempercepat keputusan pembelian pengguna Shopee.

title: சல சநதரபரமளன ‘உறஙக மறநத கமபகரணன’ கறநவலல கதபததர அமபபம மனவயல-சமகப பரமணஙகளம: Characterization and Psychological-Social Dimensions in Solai Sundaraperumal’s Novella Uranga Marantha Kumbakarnan
abstractText: Solai Sundaraperumal is one of the notable writers in modern Tamil literature who has documented social realism, the lives of marginalized people, and the subtle movements of human emotions within a rural setting. His novella Uranga Marantha Kumbakarnangal (Manasu), set in the village of Navalankudi, realistically portrays human weaknesses, mental health issues, class struggles, complexities in family relationships, and social awareness. This research article provides an in-depth analysis of the characterization of the major characters in the novella, namely Chinnasamy, Thangam, Appunu, Sevathi, Maruthayi, and Rajamani. Furthermore, it examines the author’s expression of social responsibility, parent-child relationships, societal attitudes towards persons with disabilities, feminist perspectives, and rural development through these characters. The study explores these themes from literary and sociological perspectives, highlighting the author’s concern for marginalized communities and the social realities of rural life.

title: ROLE OF SHODHANA CHIKITSA IN THE MANAGEMENT OF VATARAKTA: AN AYURVEDIC REVIEW
abstractText: Vatarakta, also termed Vatashonita in classical literature, is a distinctive disorder involving the simultaneous vitiation of Vata Dosha and Rakta Dhatu. The classical pathogenesis describes an interaction between aggravated Vata and vitiated Rakta, with obstruction of the normal movement of Vata by Rakta and subsequent aggravation of both factors. Clinically, the condition is described with pain, tenderness, burning, discoloration, swelling and functional disturbance, particularly in the extremities. Ayurveda recommends an individualized therapeutic approach according to Dosha predominance, disease stage, site, tissue involvement and strength of the patient. Shodhana Chikitsa forms an important component of this approach and includes Mridu Virechana, Basti and, in selected presentations, Raktamokshana. Snehana is described as a preparatory and therapeutic measure, while Basti receives particular emphasis in the classical management of Vatarakta. This review looks at these traditional methods and discusses how they apply to contemporary Ayurvedic practice. The available recent clinical literature is also taken into account, even though it is acknowledged that Vatarakta should not be automatically equated with gout and that current clinical studies remain heterogeneous. The review highlights the need for tailored practices and improved clinical trials that integrate standardized Ayurvedic evaluation with objective outcome measures. title: AYURVEDIC AND MODERN MANAGEMENT OF VEGAAVASTHA AND AVEGAVASTHA OF APASMAR: A REVIEW STUDY
abstractText: Apasmara, in Ayurvedic classics seems to be identical with description of epilepsy in modern medicine. Epilepsy is the second most common neurological disease. Epilepsy affects 1% of the world’s population a most common serious disorder of the brain, greatly impacting on the quality of life of individuals. In Apasmar there is imbalance in three doshas Vata, Pitta, Kapha singly or all three of them together. So, the present conceptual study helps to understand the disease of the Modern era by the Ayurvedic perspective and contributes in the Integrative approach in the management of Apasmara or Epilepsy.

title: THE CONCEPT OF DHARNIYA VEGA AND ITS IMPORTANCE TO MAINTANACE OF HEALTHY AND HAPPY LIFE
abstractText: Dharniya Vega, described in Ayurveda, refers to the voluntary suppression of harmful mental, verbal, and physical urges to maintain health and ethical conduct. Classical Ayurveda texts, particularly the Charak Samhita Sutra sthan chapter 7, Vega and types of Dharniya Vega, emphasize that controlling negative emotions such as anger (Krodha), greed (Lobha), jealousy (Irshya), excessive attachment (Raha), harsh speech and unethical, psychological, and moral health failure to regulate these impulses may contribute to psychosomatic disorders, emotional instability, and impaired social functioning. From a neuroscientific perspective, Dharniya Vega closely parallels the neural mechanisms of emotional regulation, executive control, and behavioral inhibition mediated by the prefrontal cortex, limbic system, hippocampus, and hypothalamus. Integrating Ayurvedic wisdom with contemporary neuroscience provides a holistic framework for understanding emotional regulation offering valuable insights into disease prevention, mental resilience, and the promotion of overall health and quality of life.

title: INTEGRATED AYURVEDIC MANAGEMENT OF PARTIAL URETHRAL STRICTURE WITH ASSOCIATED SCIATICA – A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Urethral stricture is a chronic urological disorder characterized by urethral narrowing, resulting in poor urinary flow and recurrent urinary tract infections. Conventional approaches such as urethral dilatation and urethroplasty often have limited success and high recurrence rates. In Ayurveda, this condition resembles Mutraghata, predominantly caused by Vata vitiation, in which Vasti Chikitsa is emphasized as a primary therapy. A 32-year-old male patient with partial urethral stricture, hypotonic bladder, and lumbar spondylosis presented with burning micturition, increased frequency, and low back pain. The treatment was planned in three phases. The integrated approach combining Matra Vasti and Uttaravasti with internal and external Ayurvedic therapies effectively addressed urethral stricture, hypotonic bladder and associated neurogenic symptoms, highlighting potential for conservative management in refractory cases. It exert effects at the cellular level by correlating Ayurvedic dosha-dhatu-srotas dynamics with modern pharmacokinetics, neurophysiology, and anti-fibrotic mechanisms.

title: ANATOMICAL INDICATORS OF DEERGHAYU (LONGEVITY)
abstractText: Ayu (lifespan) has remained an enduring focus of inquiry across classical Ayurvedic scholarship and contemporary biogerontology. Within classical Samhitas, particularly Charaka Samhita (Sharira Sthana and Vimana Sthana) and Sushruta Samhita (Sutrasthana), the estimation of lifespan is prioritized prior to therapeutic intervention. Classical authors classified longevity into Deerghayu (long lifespan), Madhyamayu (moderate lifespan), and Alpayu (short lifespan). While contemporary medicine evaluates longevity through physiological parameters, biomarkers, and genetic architecture, ancient anatomical masters formulated a comprehensive somatic appraisal scheme based on structural morphology (Anga-Pratyanga Sharir), somatic symmetry (Pramana and Samhanana), deep tissue concealedness (Gudha Sandhi-Sira Snayu), and tissue excellence (Dhatu Sara). This review presents a critical, doctoral-level anatomical synthesis of Deerghayu Lakshana (morphological indicators of longevity) extracted from classical literature and evaluates them through modern functional anatomy, developmental biology (Developmental Origins of Health and Disease - DOHaD), biomechanics, and anthropometric science. The integration of ancient observational morphology with contemporary structural science provides a robust baseline for morpho-phenotypic longevity appraisal and constitution-guided predictive medicine.

title: AI-DRIVEN DIGITAL MARKETING STRATEGIES IN THE PHARMACEUTICAL INDUSTRY: OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES, AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
abstractText: Pharmaceutical marketing is being reshaped by the growing use of digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) in communication, customer engagement, and commercial decision-making. Promotion that once relied almost entirely on medical representatives, face-to-face physician visits, product detailing, and printed material is now supplemented, and in some cases reshaped, by digital platforms, social media, e-detailing, webinars, data analytics, and omnichannel communication. This review looks at how AI is being applied to pharmaceutical digital marketing, with particular attention to machine learning, predictive analytics, segmentation of customers and healthcare professionals, personalized communication, customer relationship management, generative AI, and omnichannel engagement. Evidence from the published literature suggests that digital channels widen the reach and flexibility of pharmaceutical communication, while AI adds the ability to analyse large datasets, anticipate behaviour, segment audiences, and personalize content at scale. At the same time, this shift brings its own set of problems: data privacy, inconsistent data quality, algorithmic bias, the risk of misinformation, limited transparency, regulatory compliance, and the continued need for human oversight all surface repeatedly in the literature. Empirical studies also indicate that digital engagement can shape how healthcare professionals are communicated with, influence prescribing-related behaviour, and affect consumer attitudes, though the size of this effect depends heavily on the channel, audience, and therapeutic area involved. Taken together, the evidence points toward a future in which human expertise, digital communication, and AI-supported decision-making work alongside one another rather than one replacing the other. For this model to be sustainable, pharmaceutical marketing will need to be built on responsible implementation, ethical communication, evidence-based content, and clear governance.

title: A REVIEW ON BIOLOGICAL CHARACTERIZATION OF ISATIN ANALOGUES
abstractText: Isatin (1H-indole-2,3-dione) is a versatile heterocyclic scaffold widely explored in medicinal chemistry due to its broad spectrum of biological activities. Structural modification of isatin leads to numerous analogues exhibiting significant pharmacological properties, including antimicrobial, anticancer, antiviral, anticonvulsant, and anti-inflammatory activities. The biological characterization of these analogues involves in vitro, in vivo, and computational approaches to understand structure–activity relationships (SAR), molecular targets, and mechanisms of action. This review summarizes recent advances in the biological evaluation of isatin derivatives, highlighting their therapeutic potential and future perspectives in drug discovery.

title: MANAGEMENT OF VICHARCHIKA (ECZEMA) - AN AYURVEDIC APPROACH
abstractText: In classical Ayurvedic literature, Vicharchika is described under Kshudrakustha (skin disorders) and can be clinically correlated with Eczema or Atopic Dermatitis as described in modern medicine. It is encountered by Ayurvedic Dermatologists characterized with symptoms namely Kandu, Srava, Pidika and Shyava Varna. Eczema (also called atopic dermatitis) is characterized by dry itchy skin with areas of poorly demarcated erythema and scale. In the acute phase eczema may be vesicular and oozing, In the chronic phase it may become hyperpigmented and lichenified (thickened). Excoriations (scratch marks) are frequently seen. The modern science has greatly advanced, particularly in dermatology but there are no specific medicaments for sure of eczema but symptomatic treatments like steroids are used, but they produce serious side effects like nephrotoxicity, osteoporosis, skin cancer etc. In contrast, Ayurvedic management involves a comprehensive therapeutic approach encompassing Shodhana Chikitsa (purificatory therapies), Shamana Chikitsa (palliative treatment), and Sthanika Chikitsa (local applications), supported by appropriate Pathya Ahara (dietary regulation) and Pathya Vihara (lifestyle modification). Vicharchika is a chronic dermatological condition whose prevalence has increased in recent years due to globalization, changing lifestyle patterns, and environmental factors. Owing to its recurrent nature, the disease significantly affects the quality of life of affected individuals. Despite the availability of various treatment modalities, long-term remission with minimal recurrence remains a therapeutic challenge. Ayurveda emphasizes a preventive and holistic approach to achieve sustainable disease control. This review aims to critically analyze and compare the management of Vicharchika from Ayurvedic and modern medical perspectives, highlighting the significance of the integrative and preventive principles of Ayurveda in the effective management of the disease.

title: KEY STARTING MATERIALS IN PHARMACEUTICAL MANUFACTURING: REGULATORY BOUNDARIES, IMPURITY CONTROL, AND SUPPLY-CHAIN RESILIENCE
abstractText: Key starting materials (KSMs) sit at an awkward and consequential point in drug-substance manufacturing. They are usually bought as ordinary chemical intermediates, yet they mark the place where full good manufacturing practice (GMP) begins, they carry their own impurities into the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) process, and they often depend on a handful of upstream suppliers that the API manufacturer has never audited. This review brings these three threads together. We summarise how ICH Q7 and Q11 define and bound the starting material, and why regulators question designations made too close to the final molecule. We then discuss impurity fate and purge, with attention to mutagenic, nitrosamine, azido, elemental and solvent-related risks, and outline a proportionate analytical control strategy illustrated with methods developed in our own laboratories. The supply-chain sections examine hidden multi-tier dependency, the limits of "China-plus-one" sourcing that stops at the API stage, petrochemical and logistics exposure, and recent policy responses in India, Europe and the United States. We close with practical measures (risk-based supplier qualification, dual sourcing with real technical comparability, strategic inventory, backward integration, continuous-flow manufacturing and digital visibility) and a five-stage governance framework that treats KSM management as a shared quality, regulatory, technical and supply-chain responsibility rather than a purchasing task.

title: ABEEJATVA AS A CAUSE OF VANDHYATVA: AN AYURVEDIC APPRAISAL OF ANOVULATORY FEMALE INFERTILITY IN THE LIGHT OF GARBHA SAMBHAVA SAMAGRI
abstractText: Childlessness remains one of the most distressing conditions a couple can face, and in nearly one-third of infertile women the underlying problem lies in the failure to ovulate. Ayurveda explains conception as the outcome of four co-operating factors — Ritu (the proper time), Kshetra (the field), Ambu (nourishment) and Beeja (the seed) — and a defect in any of them may lead to Vandhyatva. When the female seed, Beeja-rupa Artava, is not formed or not released, the condition is described by terms such as Abeejatva, Nashtartava and Beejopaghata; this closely parallels anovulation in modern gynaecology. The present article examines these classical descriptions, traces their roots in Agni, Rasa Dhatu, Artavavaha Srotas and Apana Vayu, and places them alongside the current endocrine understanding of anovulation. A stage-wise line of treatment is proposed — Nidana Parivarjana, Ama Pachana and Agni Deepana, Shodhana with emphasis on Basti and Uttara Basti, Artavajanana and Garbhasthapaka drugs, and Pathya — along with the probable mode of action of the principal formulations. Seen through the Garbha Sambhava Samagri framework, Abeejatva emerges as a correctable, metabolism-linked disorder for which Ayurveda offers a rational and gentle therapeutic approach.

title: ROLE OF ASCHYOTANA IN NETRA ROGA: A REVIEW OF ITS CLASSICAL BASIS, TYPES AND CLINICAL RELEVANCE
abstractText: Aschyotana is a local therapeutic procedure described in Ayurveda for the management of several Netra Rogas (ocular isorders). It involves instillation of medicated liquid into the open eye in a controlled manner. Classical Ayurvedic texts describe Aschyotana among the important initial measures in eye care and discuss its use according to the doshic predominance, symptoms and stage of disease. Depending on the formulation and clinical indication, it is traditionally used to support cleansing, comfort and relief in selected conditions such as Abhishyanda and other inflammatory or irritative presentations. The procedure requires careful selection of medicine, dose, temperature, timing and patient suitability. This review summarises the classical basis of Aschyotana, its broad types, dose-related principles, procedure, possible therapeutic rationale and relevance in contemporary Shalakya Tantra practice. Ayurvedic descriptions provide a traditional framework; however, ocular medicines must be prepared to appropriate sterile standards and should be used under qualified clinical supervision. Aschyotana should not delay urgent ophthalmic assessment in severe pain, injury, reduced vision or suspected infection.

title: PRIMARY DYSMENORRHEA: AN OVERVIEW
abstractText: Dysmenorrhea is a common gynecological condition characterized by painful menstruation, usually presenting with lower abdominal cramps and may be associated with backache, nausea, headache, fatigue, and other systemic symptoms. It can adversely affect daily activities, academic performance, work, and overall quality of life.

title: TAMRA AS NANO-PARTICLES IN GARAVISHA CHIKITSA
abstractText: Garavisha is considered as one of the forms of Kritrima visha (artificially prepared poison) which is prepared by the combination of two or more poisonous or non-poisonous substances and ultimately affects the whole body by vitiating all the Dhatus (tissues) in the body. It can go to such extent that it alleviates the Dhatus drastically which in turn could prove fatal.

title: ADVANCED LIPOSOMAL CO-DELIVERY STRATEGIES FOR SYNERGISTIC ANTI-INFLAMMATORY THERAPY
abstractText: Inflammation is a complex physiological response associated with the progression of numerous acute and chronic diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis, pulmonary disorders, neurodegenerative conditions, and cardiovascular diseases. Although conventional anti-inflammatory therapies such as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs): corticosteroids, and immunosuppressive agents are widely used, their long-term administration is often limited by poor bioavailability, rapid metabolism, systemic toxicity, non-specific tissue distribution, and severe adverse effects. To overcome these limitations, liposomal nanocarrier systems have emerged as promising drug delivery platforms due to their biocompatibility, biodegradability, controlled release behavior, and targeting potential. Among these systems, dual drug-loaded liposomes have gained considerable attentionfor their ability to simultaneously deliver two therapeutic agents with complementary mechanisms of action, thereby enhancing synergistic anti-inflammatory efficacy while reducing toxicity and dosing frequency. This review highlights recent advances in dual drug-loaded liposomal systems developed for synergistic anti-inflammatory therapy. It discusses the structural organization, composition, classification, and formulation strategies of liposomes, including thin-film hydration, reverse-phase evaporation, ethanol injection, and active loading methods. Important physicochemical characterization parameters such as particle size, zeta potential, entrapment efficiency, drug release behavior, and stability are also summarized. Particular emphasis is placed on the co-delivery of synthetic anti-inflammatory drugs with natural bioactive compounds, antioxidants, immunomodulators, and nucleic acid therapeutics for simultaneous modulation of inflammatory pathways including NF-κB, MAPK, COX-2, cytokine signaling, and oxidative stress-mediated mechanisms. Furthermore, recent in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrating enhanced therapeutic efficacy, controlled drug release, reduced inflammatory cytokine production, and targeted accumulation at inflamed tissues are critically discussed. The review also addresses current challenges associated with large-scale manufacturing, formulation stability, regulatory approval, and clinical translation. Overall, dual drug-loaded liposomal systems represent highly promising nanotherapeutic platforms for the development of safer, more effective, and targeted anti-inflammatory therapies in the future.

title: A CRITICAL REVIEW OF THE ROLE OF PANCHAKARMA PROCEDURES IN HAIR AND HAIR HEALTH
abstractText: Hair is an important appendage of the skin that contributes not only to physical appearance but also to thermoregulation, sensory perception, and protection against environmental factors. Hair growth is a dynamic biological process regulated by genetic, hormonal, nutritional, neural, vascular, and immunological factors. Disturbances in these regulatory mechanisms lead to various hair disorders such as alopecia, premature graying, and excessive hair shedding, which significantly affect an individual's quality of life. Ayurveda describes Kesha (hair) as the Mala of Asthi Dhatu and emphasizes the importance of balanced Tridosha, healthy Dhatus, and proper nourishment for maintaining healthy hair. Various Ayurvedic procedures including Nasya Karma, Shiroabhyanga, Shirodhara, Shiro Pichu, Shiro Basti, Shiro Lepa, Prachanna, and Raktamokshana have traditionally been employed to improve scalp health and promote hair growth. Modern scientific evidence suggests that these procedures enhance local blood circulation, improve nutrient delivery, reduce oxidative stress, modulate neuroendocrine responses, and improve follicular function. This review integrates contemporary understanding of hair physiology with classical Ayurvedic concepts and discusses the probable mechanisms by which Ayurvedic procedures support hair growth and scalp health.

authors.name: Dr. Ravikanth Shilavanthar*1 PG Scholar, Dr. Venkanna S. Kanthi Md (Ayu) Professor and Hod2, Dr. Vijaykumar Math³ Associate Professor

title: ROLE OF SHODHANA CHIKITSA (VAMANA AND VIRECHANA KARMA) IN THE MANAGEMENT OF EKAKUSHTHA W.S.R. TO PSORIASIS: A REVIEW
abstractText: Background: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated, inflammatory skin disease with a relapsing course, affecting about 2–3% of the population in many regions. It causes considerable physical, psychological and social burden. In Ayurveda, its clinical features closely resemble Ekakushtha, a Kshudra Kushtha of Vata–Kapha predominance, described with the cardinal features Asvedana, Mahavastu and Matsyashakalopama. Aim: To review the classical concept of Ekakushtha and critically analyse the role of Shodhana Chikitsa — particularly Vamana and Virechana Karma — in its management, with correlation to modern understanding of psoriasis. Materials and methods: Brihattrayi, Laghuttrayi and their commentaries were reviewed for Nidana, Samprapti and Chikitsa of Kushtha and Ekakushtha. Standard dermatology texts and indexed literature were reviewed for the pathogenesis and management of psoriasis. Conclusion: The classics give primacy to repeated Shodhana in Kushtha because Doshas eliminated by Samshodhana do not recur. Vamana addresses the Kapha component responsible for Mahavastu and scaling, while Virechana addresses Pitta–Rakta Dushti and helps prevent relapse. Shodhana followed by Shamana and Rasayana offers a rational, holistic approach to psoriasis, which needs to be validated through well-designed clinical trials.

title: EFFICACY OF HARIDRA KHANDA AS PRINCIPAL SHAMANA CHIKITSA, AND LOCAL APPLICATION OF ERANDA PATRA IN MANAGEMENT OF TAMAKA SHWASA (BRONCHIAL ASTHMA) - A SINGLE CASE STUDY
abstractText: Ayurveda represents a time-honoured system of traditional medicine originating in ancient India. The medical system of Ayurveda encompasses a wide spectrum of treatment modalities tailored to individual pathology. Bronchial asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease characterized by recurrent episodes of wheezing, breathlessness, chest tightness, and cough. In Ayurveda, it is correlated with Tamaka Shwasa, a disorder predominantly involving Vata and Kapha Dosha affecting the Pranavaha Srotas. This single case study describes the successful Ayurvedic management of a patient diagnosed with moderate bronchial asthma using Haridra Khanda as the Principal Shamana Chikitsa, and local application of Eranda Patra for 30 days. Clinical assessment was performed using symptom severity scores, frequency of Asthma Attacks, breath-holding time (BHT), Peak Expiratory Flow Rate (PEFR), and spirometry assessment. Following treatment, the patient demonstrated marked improvement in respiratory symptoms, including reduction in wheezing and dyspnoea, improved exercise tolerance and sleep quality, along with significant improvement in pulmonary function. The findings suggest that the combined use of Shamana Chikitsa and local application of Eranda Patra may be an effective Ayurvedic therapeutic approach for the management of Tamaka Shwasa.

title: A CONCEPTUAL REVIEW OF PRAMEHA ACCORDING TO AYURVEDA AND CONTEMPORARY SCIENCE
abstractText: Prameha is enumerated among the Ashtau Mahagada — the eight gravest and most difficult-to-cure disorders — a placement that itself conveys the seriousness our Acharyas attached to the disease.[1] Etymologically Prameha (Pra + Mih) signifies Prabhuta (excessive) and Avila (turbid) mutrata, the twin cardinal feature of the disease.[2] In essence it is a Kleda-pradhana, Medovaha-srotodushti-janya vyadhi born chiefly of Santarpana (over-nourishment), a sedentary and sleep-indulgent mode of living, and hereditary predisposition. The classics describe twenty varieties of Prameha — ten Kaphaja, six Pittaja and four Vataja — graded in severity, with Madhumeha, a Vataja type, representing the terminal and most intractable stage into which neglected Pramehas ultimately culminate.[3] The Samprapti turns upon vitiation of Kapha and Meda obstructing the channels (Avarana), or upon Dhatukshaya driving Vata, with Vata acting as the Anubandha dosha in both pathways. In contemporary terms the Prameha spectrum corresponds broadly to the continuum of obesity, metabolic syndrome, prediabetes, diabetes mellitus and allied urological disorders. The present review consolidates the Nidana, Purvarupa, Rupa, Samprapti, Bheda, Upadrava, Sadhya-asadhyata and Chikitsa-siddhanta of Prameha from the Brihattrayi, correlated with modern understanding, so as to clarify its pathogenesis and to frame the scope and limitations of its management.

title: "AYURVEDIC MANAGEMENT OF DADRU KUSHTA W.S.R TINEA CORPORIS": A CASE SERIES
abstractText: Background: Kushta is described by Acharya Charaka among the Ashtomahagada and encompasses a broad spectrum of dermatological disorders. Dadru, a subtype of Kshudra Kushta characterized predominantly by Kandu (itching), Raga (erythema), Piḍaka (papules) and Mandala (annular lesions). Its clinical presentation shows considerable correlation with tinea corporis, a superficial dermatophytic infection characterized by annular, erythematous, scaly and pruritic lesions. Dadru Kushta is predominantly Kapha Pitta Doṣa in presentation, with involvement of Rasa, Rakta, Kleda, Ama as important Duṣhya. Objective: To evaluate the efficacy of Virechanottara Edgajadi lepa along with Shamana aushadhi in managing Dadru kushta (Tinea corporis). Methodology: Prospective, open-label, uncontrolled, incidental case series study. 5 subjects diagnosed with Dadru kushta (Tinea corporis) were treated with Deepana pachana with Trikatu churna, Virechana with Trivruttdai yoga, shamana Aushadhi includes Edagajadi lepa, Vidangadi yoga and Allum soup Result: The intervention demonstrated significant improvement in all assessed subjective parameters (Kandu, Raga, Pidaka and Mandala). Conclusion: The combination of Vidangadi yoga and Edagajadi Lepa demonstrated significant therapeutic efficacy in the management of Dadru kushta (Tinea Corporis).

title: EFFECT OF BHUJANGASANA (COBRA POSE) IN ALPARTAVA (HYPOMENORRHEA): A REVIEW
abstractText: A woman's health plays a crucial role in the welfare of her family, society, and culture. Various physiological changes take place at birth and more significant transformations occurring during puberty of female. However, modern lifestyle factors such as inactivity, poor diet, and stress can disrupt the normal functioning of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian-uterine axis, leading to a range of gynaecological issues. Hypomenorrhea is one of the menstrual disorders characterized by an abnormally light menstrual flow. The amount of bleeding is noticeably less than what is typical for the individual, and in some cases, it may present as mere spotting or last for only a short time—often under two days. In Ayurveda, hypomenorrhea is referred to as Alpartava. Classical texts describe most menstrual disorders under the categories of Ashta Artava Dushti, Artava Kshaya, Anartava, Kashtartava, and Nashta Artava. Alpa Artava is often observed as a symptom associated with various reproductive disorders. Considering its clinical features, it can be closely correlated with the condition known as hypomenorrhea. In modern medicine, the available treatments for symptoms often do not address the underlying cause of the condition. Moreover, they can lead to side effects such as weight gain, reduced libido, headaches, mood swings, and can also be expensive. Ayurveda Classics suggest that yoga can help manage Alpartava (hypomenorrhea). One such yoga pose, Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose), is known to enhance spinal flexibility, strengthen the back and uterine muscles, and promote better blood flow during menstruation.

title: EFFECT OF JUNK FOOD ON RASA DHATU
abstractText: Ayurveda explains health (Swasthya) in terms of the balance of Doshas, proper functioning of Agni, appropriate formation of Dhatus and Malas, and a settled state of the Atma, Indriya, and Manas. Among the seven Dhatus described in classical texts — Rasa, Rakta, Mamsa, Meda, Asthi, Majja, and Shukra — Rasa Dhatu is especially important because it is the first Dhatu formed after digestion. It is responsible for sustaining life by providing nutrition, vitality (Bala), mental clarity, emotional balance, complexion (Varna), and overall well-being (Prinana).

title: GARBHA VARNA UTPATTI: AN ANALYTICAL STUDY OF AYURVEDA SIDDHANTA AND MODERN EMBRYOLOGY PERSPECTIVES
abstractText: Varna (skin color and complexion) is an important diagnostic and prognostic factor in Ayurveda, extending beyond pigmentation to radiance, lustre, and vitality. But with the concept of Garbha Varna Utpatti (origin of fetal skin color) described by Acharya Charaka, Sushruta, Kashyapa, and others, specifying and attributing skin color to Panchamahabhuta, Shukra-Shonita, maternal diet, regimen, psychological state, and hereditary factors. Classical treatises also highlight hereditary and spiritual determinants (Beeja, Beejabhaga, Piturja, Matruja, Atmaja, Satmyaja bhava). Contemporary science explains skin pigmentation primarily through melanogenesis, genetic regulation, embryological skin development, and environmental influences. This article attempts to understand Ayurveda concepts with embryology, biochemistry, and genetics, thereby presenting an integrative framework for understanding of fetal skin color and identify areas for further research. Understanding Garbha Varna Utpatti through both Ayurveda and modern science also provides opportunities for integrative approaches to maternal-fetal care (maternal care, fetal dermatology, and Ayurvedic nutrigenomics).

title: COMPARATIVE CLINICAL STUDY OF VISARPA WITH JALOKAVACHARANA AND AUDUMBAR LEPA: AN AYURVEDIC CLINICAL EVALUATION
abstractText: Background: Visarpa is a rapidly spreading inflammatory skin disorder described extensively in the Ayurvedic classics. It is predominantly caused by vitiation of Pitta, Rakta, and associated Dhatus, producing symptoms such as erythema, burning sensation, pain, vesicular eruptions, oedema, and rapid spread of lesions. Based on clinical similarities, Visarpa can be correlated with Herpes Zoster (Shingles). Since Rakta Dushti is the principal pathological factor, Acharya Sushruta has advocated Raktamokshana as the treatment of choice. Jalaukavacharana (Leech Therapy), a form of Raktamokshana, is considered the safest procedure for Pittaja disorders, while Audumbar Lepa possesses Pittahara, Raktaprasadana, Dahashamana, Shothahara and Vranaropana properties. Aim: To compare the clinical efficacy of Jalaukavacharana and Audumbar Lepa in the management of Visarpa (Herpes Zoster). Materials and Methods: A comparative clinical study was conducted on patients diagnosed with Visarpa/Herpes Zoster. Patients were randomly allocated into two groups. Group A received Jalaukavacharana, while Group B received topical application of Audumbar Lepa. Clinical parameters including Vedana (pain), Daha (burning sensation), Raga (erythema), Shotha (swelling), Kandu (itching), Sphota (vesicles), and overall clinical improvement were assessed before treatment, during treatment, and after completion. Statistical analysis was performed using appropriate paired and unpaired statistical tests. Results: Both interventions produced statistically significant improvement in the clinical features of Visarpa. However, Jalaukavacharana demonstrated comparatively superior relief in pain, burning sensation, erythema, oedema, and overall clinical recovery. The rapid action of leech therapy in removing vitiated blood and reducing inflammation contributed to earlier symptom relief compared with Audumbar Lepa. Conclusion: Both Jalaukavacharana and Audumbar Lepa are effective in the management of Visarpa. Jalaukavacharana showed comparatively better therapeutic efficacy and can be considered an effective Panchakarma intervention for Pitta-Rakta predominant Visarpa.

title: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF CONTAMINATION, ANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES, QUALITY CONTROL AND SAFETY
abstractText: Herbal drug formulations are increasingly used as traditional, complementary and supportive healthcare products. Although their botanical origin is often associated with natural safety, medicinal plants can accumulate potentially toxic elements from soil, irrigation water, atmospheric deposition, agricultural inputs and contaminated processing environments. Lead, cadmium, mercury and arsenic are among the most important contaminants because repeated exposure can produce neurological, renal, cardiovascular, hematological and other systemic effects. Consequently, determination of elemental contaminants is an essential part of the quality assessment of herbal medicines. This review presents an integrated discussion of the occurrence and significance of toxic elements in herbal drug formulations, environmental and manufacturing sources of contamination, plant uptake and translocation, sampling, homogenization and digestion, conventional limit tests, atomic absorption spectrometry, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry, inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, X-ray fluorescence and electrochemical approaches. It further discusses method validation, quality-control samples, calibration, blanks, recovery, detection limits, uncertainty and regulatory interpretation. A reliable analytical strategy begins with representative sampling and suitable sample preparation and ends with a scientifically justified interpretation of the measured concentration. Modern multi-element techniques provide sensitive and efficient analysis, but their performance depends on matrix control, contamination prevention and appropriate validation. Risk-based control across cultivation, procurement, processing and finished-product testing provides stronger consumer protection than reliance on a single end-product test.

title: MARMA CHIKITSA A BOON IN PRESENT ERA
abstractText: Ayurveda is the science of life. It is the oldest system of medicine in world that has a unique perspective for harmonious living. Marma is the unique concept of Ayurveda whose detailed description is mentioned in Sushruta Samhita. Marma is defined as vital point of body, the region in which there is confluence of Mansa, Sira, Snayu, Asthi and Sandhi. Pran is situated on these places naturally. Marma Chikitsa is a supreme method of Ayurvedic treatment, for whole spectrum of health disorders. Stimulation of Marma points through various technique help in the removing of blockages from the Marma points giving physical and physiological relaxation and stimulate the flow of Pran thus resulting treat the various disorders and maintain the healthy state. In the present scenario Marma Chikitsa is an immediate and permanent way of healthy living at physical, mental, emotional and spiritual levels.

title: A REVIEW ON THE ROLE OF INFLAMMATION IN SKIN CANCER AND NEW TREATMENT APPROACHES
abstractText: The rate of skin cancer has escalated rapidly over the past decade, affecting both melanoma and non-melanoma types. Skin cancers primarily consist of keratinocyte cancers, including cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, and melanoma. This review highlights recent progress in skin cancer treatments. In addition to chemotherapy, options such as immunotherapy, targeted therapy, and photodynamic therapy (PDT) are available for skin cancer. Furthermore, the combination of PDT with chemotherapy, radiation, immunotherapy, and surgery is currently being explored. This review will focus on the pathophysiology of skin cancer and existing therapies utilized in the topical treatment of skin cancers, as well as introduce novel treatments that may offer benefits for these conditions.

title: A CONCEPTUAL REVIEW OF SARPA VIJNANA AS DESCRIBED IN VISHA VAIDYA VIJNANA
abstractText: Background: Sarpa Vijnana is an important aspect of Agada Tantra, dealing with the classification and characteristics of snakes and various features related to snakebite. The availability of classical literature exclusively for Agada Tantra is limited and Visha Vaidya Vijnana, a tulu translated book provides a comprehensive account of these aspects. Hence a conceptual review of this work was undertaken to highlight its contribution to the existing knowledge of Ayurvedic toxicology. Aim: To review the concepts of Sarpa Vijnana described in Visha Vaidya Vijnana. Materials and Methods: Relevant information regarding the classification of Vamshastha, Naage, Kadambale and Kandhodi Sarpa, along with their varieties, types of fang, reproductive characteristics, movement, age determination, prognosis of bite and snakebite wounds, was collected and analysed. Conclusion: Visha Vaidya Vijnana provides a valuable classical knowledge on Sarpa Vijnana. A review of these concepts may help to explore their relevance in relation to contemporary science.

title: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW ON THAI BASIL
abstractText: Thai basil(Ocimum basilicum L.) is an aromatic medicinal and culinary herb belonging to the family Lamiaceae and is widely valued for its distinctive aroma, flavor, and diverse pharmacological properties. This review provides a comprehensive overview of Thai basil, focusing on its botanical characteristics, traditional uses, phytochemical composition, nutritional importance and therapeutic potential. The plant contain several bioactive constituents, including essential oils, phenolic compounds, flavonoids, terpenoids, and other secondary metabolites, which contribute to its antioxidant, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, antidiabetic, cardioprotective, hepatoprotective, anti-cancer, activities. Particular attention is given to major constituents such as eugenol, linalool, methyl chavicol (estragole), and rosmarinic acid, which are associated with many types of its biological effects. The review also discusses extraction methods, factor affecting phytochemical composition, and reported pharmacological activities of different plant part. In addition, the potential applications of Thai basil in pharmaceutics, neutraceutical food and cosmetics formulations are highlighted. Available scientific evidence indicates the Thai basil represent a promising sources of natural bioactive compounds, however, further standardized studies, toxicity, evaluation, clinical investigations, and quality control approaches knowledge of Thai basil and identities opportunities for future research and development of safe effective herbal product.

title: PREPARATION, PHYSICOCHEMICAL CHARACTERIZATION AND CLINICAL EFFICACY OF MANJISHTHADI TAILA IN VYANGA
abstractText: Ayurveda, the traditional system of medicine, emphasizes holistic health and the maintenance of skin through natural and lifestyle-based approaches. Among various dermatological conditions described in Ayurveda, Vyanga is characterized by painless, localized hyperpigmentation on the face, commonly associated with stress, dietary irregularities, and imbalances of Vata and Pitta doshas. In the modern era, increasing exposure to environmental pollutants and ultraviolet radiation has further contributed to the prevalence of such pigmentation disorders. Ayurvedic formulations, particularly those derived from Bhaishajya Kalpana, offer effective and safe treatment options. Manjishthadi Taila, a medicated oil prepared using Tila Taila (sesame oil) and skin-beneficial herbs like Manjishtha and Yashtimadhu, possesses antioxidant, photoprotective, and complexion-enhancing properties. The present study highlights the need for development and quality evaluation of Manjishthadi Taila as a safe and effective topical treatment for Vyanga.

title: PHARMACOLOGICAL AND MOLECULAR MECHANISM OF ACTION OF DAIDZEIN: AN UPDATED REVIEW
abstractText: Medicinal plants have proved to be of great importance since long back as they are traditionally used to make plant-derived medicines that are a good alternative to synthetic chemicals. Daidzein is one such chemical compound that belongs to the group of isoflavones and is obtained from leguminous plants, especially soy plants. Daidzein is structurally similar to human hormone estrogen due to which is also called a phytoestrogen. Daidzein is an isoflavone compound that is mostly found in glycosylated form in plants while in humans it is found in free form in the bloodstream. It is clinically used in treatment of variety of cancers. It has become quite successful in treating ovarian cancer, breast cancer, and thyroid cancer. Daidzein also possess some exquisite properties such as anti-inflammatory properties, anti-oxidant properties, and neuroprotective properties. In this paper mechanical properties of daidzein are also discussed in which daidzein has been proved as an excellent wood adhesive agent for industrial purpose. Also, daidzein is used as flame retardant and is doing good in dietary supplementations. Daidzein can be important for further pharmaceutical and industrial applications.

title: DIAGNOSIS, MANAGEMENT AND TREATMENT OF ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE
abstractText: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder and the leading cause of dementia in older adults. It impairs communication between neurons and ultimately causes neuronal death. Pathologically, it is characterised by extracellular senile plaques composed of β-amyloid (Aβ) deposits and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles composed of abnormally hyperphosphorylated tau protein. The prevalence of dementia rises sharply with age worldwide and places a heavy financial burden on society. AD arises from a complex interaction of genetic, environmental, and demographic factors. Late-onset AD is strongly influenced by advanced age and the APOE ε4 allele, whereas early-onset AD is associated with rare autosomal dominant mutations in the APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 genes. Low educational attainment, physical inactivity, poor diet, smoking, cardiovascular comorbidities, and chronic sleep disturbance are additional risk factors. Clinically, AD presents with subtle short-term memory loss, followed by executive dysfunction, agnosia, apraxia, disorientation, language impairment (aphasia), and non-cognitive symptoms. Diagnosis rests on clinical history, cognitive screening (MMSE, MoCA), physical examination, and structural neuroimaging (MRI/CT), and is further refined by the ATN biomarker framework, which includes FDG-PET, amyloid-PET, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) measurements. Current pharmacological treatment relies mainly on acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and NMDA receptor antagonists for symptomatic relief, while emerging research is examining disease-modifying immunotherapies that target the removal of Aβ plaques.

title: AN AYURVEDIC PERSPECTIVE OF DIABETIC PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY W.S.R TO MADHUMEHA UPADRAVA: A REVIEW ARTICLE
abstractText: Diabetes Mellitus (DM) is a prevalent metabolic disorder and a significant public health concern in India, contributing substantially to morbidity due to its chronic complications. Among these, Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy (DPN) is one of the most common and disabling long-term complications. Its prevalence increases with disease duration—affecting approximately 26% of patients after five years and up to 41% after ten years of diabetes. Over a lifetime, 50–66% of diabetic individuals are estimated to develop DPN. It is characterized by progressive sensory loss starting in the toes and spreading proximally, along with tingling, burning, and aching pain that negatively affects quality of life. Although medicines used for pain management provide symptomatic relief, their long-term use may be limited by adverse effects. This highlights the necessity for exploring alternative therapeutic approaches with minimal side effects; Methods: A comprehensive understanding of Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy from an Ayurvedic perspective through an in-depth literary review, incorporating insights from classical Ayurvedic texts (Samhitas) and contemporary electronic resources. Result: Ayurveda views Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy as more than just a complication of diabetes—it is understood as an expression of internal physiological imbalances. Discussion: Ayurveda emphasizes a comprehensive and personalized approach to the management of Diabetes Peripheral Neuropathy, focusing on restoring systemic balance rather than targeting isolated symptoms.

title: NITROSAMINE DRUG SUBSTANCE-RELATED IMPURITIES: COMPARATIVE FDA AND EMA REGULATORY FRAMEWORKS, ANALYTICAL CHALLENGES, AND SUPPLY IMPLICATIONS
abstractText: Nitrosamine drug substance-related impurities (NDSRIs) became a significant global concern after nitrosamines were found in angiotensin receptor blockers and other medicines. Both the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Medicines Agency (EMA) aim to reduce patient exposure to these potentially harmful impurities, but they differ in their legal authority, how they set acceptable intake (AI) limits, implementation timelines, reporting requirements, and flexibility. This review examines how the FDA and EMA currently manage NDSRI control, covering their legal foundations, how they set AI limits, assess structure-activity relationships, use the Carcinogenic Potency Categorization Approach (CPCA), conduct confirmatory testing, handle regulatory submissions, and manage products throughout their lifecycle. It also covers analytical method development, supply chain effects, and new mutagenicity testing methods, such as transgenic rodent assays and error-corrected next-generation sequencing. The review finds that FDA guidance allows product-specific flexibility when patient access is at risk. In contrast, the EMA uses a more formal process via the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) Article 5(3) opinion. Greater harmonization, better compound-specific data, and improved analytical and toxicological tools could help make global standards more consistent and protect access to important medicines.

title: ADHD IN THE DIGITAL ERA: AN AYURVEDIC PERSPECTIVE ON SCREEN EXPOSURE, LIFESTYLE AND CHILD BEHAVIOUR
abstractText: Background: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) has emerged as a significant neurodevelopmental concern globally, exacerbated in recent decades by pervasive digital screen exposure, sedentary routines, and nutritional transitions in paediatric populations. While contemporary medicine identifies prefrontal dopaminergic and noradrenergic dysregulation as central to ADHD, classical Ayurveda offers a comprehensive psycho-physiological framework to understand cognitive instability, attention deficits, and behavioural hyper-reactivity. Objective: This narrative review aims to synthesize classical Ayurvedic principles with contemporary neurobiological evidence to elucidate the impact of excessive screen exposure and lifestyle modifications on child behaviour and ADHD pathogenesis. Methods: Classical Ayurvedic texts (Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, and Ashtanga Hridaya) were critically reviewed alongside electronic databases including PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar from inception to October 2023. Relevant literature on paediatric screen media exposure, neurodevelopmental outcomes, Manovaha Srotas pathology, and Medhya interventions was analysed. Results: Excessive screen exposure constitutes a contemporary manifestation of Asatmendriyartha Samyoga (inappropriate sensory-object contact) and Prajnaparadha (intellectual blasphemy), instigating Raja-Tama imbalance and Prana-Udana Vata vitiation. These factors disrupt Dhee (acquisition/cognition), Dhriti (retention/inhibitory control), and Smriti (recall). Modern literature confirms that hyper-stimulating digital visual stimuli alter dopaminergic mesolimbic circuitry, degrade executive function, and disrupt circadian melatonin synthesis. Ayurvedic management—integrating Dinacharya (daily regimen), Satvavajaya Chikitsa (behavioural/cognitive psychotherapy), and Medhya Rasayana (nootropic formulations)—provides a holistic, neuroprotective countermeasure. Conclusion: Integrating Ayurvedic lifestyle paradigms and neuro-nutritive therapies with contemporary behavioural interventions presents a viable, integrative strategy to mitigate digital-era paediatric attentional deficits, warranting rigorous translational and clinical validation.

title: A STUDY OF PRESENT DIETARY PATTERN FOR SOME COMMON SANTARPANOTHA VYADHI
abstractText: Santarpanottha Vyadhi are a group of disorders that arise due to excessive nourishment, unhealthy dietary habits, and sedentary lifestyle, which have become increasingly prevalent in the modern era. Improper dietary practices play a significant role in the manifestation and progression of these diseases, making the assessment of present dietary patterns essential for understanding their etiopathogenesis. The present study was undertaken to evaluate the dietary patterns of patients suffering from common Santarpanottha Vyadhi and to assess their association with selected laboratory parameters. A total of 150 patients, comprising 30 patients each with Prameha, Sthoulya, Kustha, Sotha, and Pandu, were included in the study. Dietary assessment was carried out using a structured questionnaire based on Ayurvedic principles, evaluating various Santarpanottha Aharaja Nidanas. The study revealed a high incidence of disease-specific dietary Nidanas among the selected Santarpanottha Vyadhis, with notable variations in dietary habits across different disease groups. The study emphasizes that unhealthy dietary patterns remain an important contributory factor in the development and progression of Santarpanottha Vyadhis and highlights the importance of appropriate dietary modifications for their prevention and management.

title: THERAPEUTIC UTILITY OF VAMANA AND VIRECHANA IN MITI-GATING OCCUPATIONAL BIOTOXICITY AND HEAVY METAL EXPOSURE
abstractText: Modern industrial, agricultural, and artisanal sectors increasingly expose workers to chronic heavy metal toxicity (e.g., lead, mercury, cadmium, arsenic) and biological hazards. Chronic exposure leads to bioaccumulation, oxidative stress, cellular damage, and systemic organ toxicity. Conventional chelation therapies often carry risk of re-distribution toxicity, essential mineral depletion, and adverse systemic effects. Ayurveda offers a systemic bio cleansing framework through Panchakarma, specifically Vamana (therapeutic emesis) and Virechana (therapeutic purgation), designed to eliminate endotoxins (Ama) and xenobiotics (Visha) from the cellular level.

title: AYURVEDIC APPROACH TO AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: A SHORT REVIEW
abstractText: Age-related macular degeneration (ARMD) is a progressive disorder affecting the macula and may impair central vision, particularly in older adults. Ayurveda does not describe ARMD as an exact equivalent of one classical disease; however, published authors have discussed its possible clinical resemblance to selected Drishtigata Rogas, especially Pitta Vidagdha Drishti. This short narrative review summarizes Ayurvedic literature on this conceptual correlation and reported approaches such as Akshi Tarpana, Nasya and selected oral formulations. Although preliminary reports are encouraging, current evidence is limited and requires confirmation through well-designed clinical studies.

title: PANCHAKARMA AND PREVENTIVE HEALTHCARE: AN AYURVEDIC APPROACH TO COMMUNITY WELLBEING
abstractText: Preventive healthcare is increasingly recognized as an essential component of modern health systems, particularly in the context of lifestyle-related disorders, chronic diseases, psychological stress and declining quality of life. Ayurveda, with its holistic understanding of health, emphasizes preservation of health in healthy individuals and prevention and management of disease in the diseased. Within this framework, Panchakarma occupies an important position as a specialized therapeutic approach aimed at maintaining physiological equilibrium and managing aggravated Doshas through appropriately selected procedures. Classical Ayurveda describes Shodhana therapies, including Vamana, Virechana, Basti and Nasya, as physician-supervised interventions selected according to an individual's constitution, disease status, strength, season and suitability. The preventive potential of Panchakarma should not be interpreted as routine “detoxification” for every individual. Rather, it can be understood within the broader Ayurvedic framework of Dosha equilibrium, Agni, Srotas, appropriate diet, daily and seasonal regimens, and subsequent Rasayana and lifestyle measures. At the community level, Ayurveda can contribute through health education, dietary counselling, Dinacharya, Ritucharya, Prakriti-based lifestyle guidance and appropriately indicated Panchakarma services. Contemporary evidence suggests potential supportive roles for selected Ayurvedic interventions, while also highlighting the need for standardized protocols, safety monitoring and rigorous clinical research. Therefore, integrating classical knowledge with scientific evaluation can help develop safe, evidence-informed and community-oriented preventive healthcare models.

title: AYURVEDA AND THE GUT–LIVER–PANCREAS AXIS: INTEGRATING TRADITIONAL CONCEPTS WITH CONTEMPORARY INSIGHTS INTO THE MICROBIOME, METABOLISM AND INFLAMMATION
abstractText: The gut–liver–pancreas axis represents a complex bidirectional communication network connecting the gastrointestinal tract, liver and pancreas through microbial, metabolic, endocrine, neural and immune pathways. Increasing evidence indicates that alterations in gut microbiota, intestinal barrier integrity and microbial metabolites contribute to metabolic disorders including obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, microbial products and gut-derived hormones participate in the regulation of glucose and lipid metabolism, inflammation and pancreatic endocrine function. Ayurveda provides a traditional framework in which digestion and metabolism are central to health. Concepts including Agni, Āma, Doṣa, Ahara, Jatharagni and Dhātu Agni describe different aspects of digestion, transformation and systemic homeostasis. Although these concepts originate from a different theoretical framework than contemporary biomedical science, they may provide useful hypotheses for investigating the relationship between diet, gastrointestinal function, metabolism and systemic inflammation. This review explores the possible interface between Ayurvedic concepts and contemporary understanding of the gut–liver–pancreas axis, with particular emphasis on gut microbiota, intestinal barrier function, microbial metabolites, bile-acid signalling, insulin resistance and inflammatory pathways. The potential relevance of Ayurvedic dietary and lifestyle principles in metabolic health is also discussed. Importantly, traditional concepts should not be regarded as direct equivalents of modern biological entities without appropriate experimental validation. Integrating Ayurvedic clinical phenotyping with microbiome science, metabolomics and conventional metabolic biomarkers may provide a promising framework for future research in personalized and integrative medicine.

title: NEXT-GENERATION ADVANCEMENTS IN POLYMERIC MICRONEEDLES AND NANO CARRIER-MEDIATED TRANSDERMAL DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEMS
abstractText: Transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) provide several advantages over conventional oral and parenteral routes, including avoidance of gastrointestinal degradation and hepatic first-pass metabolism, improved patient compliance, and controlled drug delivery. However, the stratum corneum acts as a major barrier, limiting the passive transport of hydrophilic and high-molecular-weight therapeutic agents. This review focuses on recent advances in polymeric microneedles and nanocarrier-mediated transdermal drug delivery systems developed to overcome these skin-permeation limitations. Literature from PubMed and Scopus was reviewed with emphasis on microneedle classification, polymeric biomaterials, nanocarrier systems, drug-loading capacity, permeation mechanisms, safety, and clinical translation. Polymeric microneedles, including solid, coated, dissolving, hydrogel-forming, and hollow systems, enable controlled and minimally painful delivery by creating temporary microchannels through the stratum corneum. Nanocarriers such as liposomes, ethosomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, nanostructured lipid carriers, polymeric nanoparticles, and inorganic nanoparticles further enhance dermal and transdermal drug transport through lipid fluidization, follicular pathways, and controlled drug deposition. The integration of these technologies provides promising opportunities for delivering macromolecules, vaccines, and localized therapeutics. Future developments involving stimuli-responsive systems, wearable biosensors, artificial intelligence, microfluidics, and personalized manufacturing may further enhance transdermal therapy. Despite challenges related to manufacturing scalability, regulatory standardization, and long-term biocompatibility, advanced microneedle and nanocarrier platforms have considerable potential for clinical translation and personalized drug delivery. Background: Traditional transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) provide a non-invasive, patient-compliant route that avoids gastrointestinal degradation and hepatic first-pass metabolism. However, the impermeable lipid matrix of the stratum corneum strictly limits the passive transport of molecules to those possessing specific hydrophobic profiles and low molecular weights. Objective: This comprehensive review examines contemporary physical and chemical breakthrough technologies, with specific focus on polymeric microneedles (MNs) and nanocarrier-facilitated delivery platforms engineered to overcome these macro-molecular transport constraints. Methodology: A systematic screening of literature from the PubMed and Scopus databases (spanning foundational models through 2026) was conducted to evaluate the mechanical structural properties, biopolymer selections, and systemic pharmacokinetics of advanced skin-permeation platforms. Results: Polymeric microneedles (dissolving, hydrogel-forming, and stimuli-responsive types) demonstrate precise disruption of the stratum corneum without contacting dermally located pain-sensitive nerve endings. Concurrently, lipidic, polymeric, and inorganic nanocarriers capitalize on hair follicles and transient lipid fluidization to deposit high-molecular-weight biologics, vaccines, and localized therapeutics. Conclusion: Combining active mechanical microneedles with target-specific nanocarriers represents the vanguard of modern personalized diagnostics and therapeutics, bridging laboratory innovation with clinical scale-up paradigms.

title: MANAGEMENT OF DYSLIPIDEMIA THROUGH AYURVEDIC THERAPY AND ORAL MEDICATIONS: A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Dyslipidemia is a common metabolic disorder associated with lifestyle diseases such as pancreatitis, fatty liver, and cardiovascular conditions. In the Indian population, elevated cholesterol levels affect approximately 25–30% of urban and 15–20% of rural individuals. In Ayurveda, dyslipidemia is correlated with Medovaha Srotodushti and Medoroga, reflecting derangement in fat metabolism channels. This case report presents a 36-year-old male with overweight status, excessive perspiration, heaviness in the body, and back pain for one year. The treatment protocol included Virechan (therapeutic purgation), Basti (Medicated enema), Udavartan (Powder massage), followed by Shaman chikitsa (oral palliative) care. Post-treatment assessment using lipid profile and body weight measurements demonstrated marked improvements in symptoms alongside reduction in cholesterol levels and weight.

title: SIRA, DHAMANI AND SROTAS: A CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF THEIR DISTINCT IDENTITY WITH CONTEMPORARY ANATOMICAL CORRELATION
abstractText: Sira, Dhamani and Srotas occupy an important place in Ayurvedic Rachana Shareera. All three are associated with Vahana and movement of different substances within the Shareera, which has resulted in considerable discussion regarding their individual identity and possible contemporary anatomical correlations. A commonly used explanation equates Dhamani with arteries, Sira with veins and Srotas with channels or capillaries. Although useful for introductory understanding, this approach does not satisfactorily explain the complete classical description. Acharya Charaka differentiates these terms through their characteristic activities - Dhmana, Sarana and Sravana. Acharya Sushruta gives detailed accounts of Sira Sankhya, Dhamani Vibhaga and their distribution, and specifically discusses the distinction between Sira, Dhamani and Srotas. The present literary review analyses their classical descriptions with emphasis on Nirukti, Sankhya, Mula, Prasara, Karma and clinical significance, followed by cautious correlation with contemporary vascular anatomy, microcirculation, lymphatics, ducts and other transport pathways. The review suggests that Dhamani has a close functional resemblance to pulsatile distributing pathways, Sira has a strong vascular and conducting association, while Srotas is a broader system-oriented concept concerned with transport of Prana, Anna, Udaka, Dhatu-poshaka amsha and Mala. These correlations are contextual and should not replace the original Ayurvedic concepts.

title: BEYOND CONVENTIONAL FORMULATIONS: THE EXPANDING ROLE OF SELF-EMULSIFYING DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEMS
abstractText: Lipid-based formulations known as self-emulsifying drug delivery systems (SEDDS) are intended to increase the oral bioavailability of medications that are poorly soluble in water. When these systems are exposed to gastrointestinal fluids and gently stirred, oils, surfactants, co-surfactants, and co-solvents spontaneously create fine oil-in-water emulsions. This procedure improves intestine absorption, medication solubility, and dissolution, which increases therapeutic efficacy. Excipients must be carefully chosen for SEDDS formulation based on the drug's physicochemical characteristics. Several solidification techniques, including capsule filling, spray drying, spray chilling, adsorption onto carriers, and Lyophilization, are utilized to create solid SEDDS in order to address stability and handling concerns related to liquid systems. To assure quality and performance, SEDDS are evaluated using droplet size analysis, zeta potential, thermodynamic stability tests, Dispersibility testing, viscosity measurement, and in vitro drug release studies. title: IDENTIFICATION OF β-SITOSTEROL IN A LIPOPHILIC FRACTION OF KHAYA GRANDIFOLIOLA C. DC. (MELIACEAE) BY SPECTROSCOPIC ANALYSIS
abstractText: β-Sitosterol is a widely distributed plant sterol of interest in the phytochemical characterization of natural resources. This study aimed to isolate and spectroscopically characterize a sterol compound from the dichloromethane extract of the stem bark of Khaya grandifoliola C. DC. (Meliaceae), collected in April 2025 in Ahougnassou-Allahou, Tiébissou Department, Côte d’Ivoire. After drying and pulverization, the plant material was subjected to successive maceration with n-hexane, dichloromethane, and ethyl acetate. The dichloromethane extract was then fractionated by silica gel column chromatography, with fractions monitored by thin-layer chromatography (TLC). The isolated compound was characterized by combining proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR), carbon-13 nuclear magnetic resonance (13C NMR), and DEPT-135 spectroscopic data. The 1H NMR spectrum showed an olefinic proton signal at approximately δH 5.35 ppm and a multiplet at δH 3.5-3.6 ppm, consistent with a proton associated with a carbon-carbon double bond and a proton attached to an oxygen-bearing carbon, respectively. The 13C NMR spectrum displayed two olefinic carbon signals at δC 140.8 and 121.7 ppm, together with an oxygenated carbon signal at δC 71.8 ppm. These signals, considered alongside the characteristic aliphatic profile, are consistent with the reported NMR data for β-sitosterol. Accordingly, the spectroscopic findings support the tentative identification of the isolated compound as β-sitosterol. Nevertheless, in the absence of two-dimensional NMR data, mass spectrometric analysis, and an assessment of the isolate’s purity, this structural assignment remains provisional and requires further confirmation.

title: HEMORRHOIDS AND HOMOEOPATHY: AN OVERVIEW OF THERAPEUTIC APPROACH AND MANAGEMENT
abstractText: Hemorrhoids are common anorectal condition with great impact on quality of life of the population. It is characterized by rectal bleeding, pain, itching and discomfort. Homeopathic literature provides detailed description of medicines for hemorrhoids to prescribe on the basis individual approach. This article discusses the selected homoeopathic medicines and their indication. Medicines frequently described in classical literature are Aesculus hippocastanum, Hamamelis virginiana, Nux vomica, Aloe socotrina, Ratanhia, Collinsonia canadensis, Nitric acidum and Sulphur. Randomized controlled trials published in 2024 and 2026 have investigated individualized homeopathic intervention and reported favourable outcomes. This review highlights the difference among the indications of the homeopathic medicines in cases of hemorrhoids.

title: AYURVEDIC UNDERSTANDING OF KATIGRAHA: A REVIEW ARTICLE
