title: A LITERARY REVIEW ON THE ROLE OF RASADISHADBHAVAS IN GARBHAVRIDDHI
abstractText: In Ayurvedic embryology (Garbha shareera) the formation and development of Garbha, are attributed to the synergy of six procreative factors known as shad garbhakara bhavas. These are Matruja, Pitruja, Atmaja, Rasaja, Satmyaja, Satvaja. The conglomeration of all six factors is essential for the creation of healthy progeny while matruja, pitruja, atmaja factors are considered predetermined at conception, the rasaja, satmyaja, sattvaja factors can be influenced by the mother’s life style and diet during pregnancy to ensure optimal fetal outcomes. Each procreative factors (shad garbhakarabhavas) is assigned with a certain organogenesis / functional /psychological phenomenon to develop the foetus during intrauterine life. If there is impairment in these factors leads to physical, functional/psychological defects which can be contributed by the respective factor. Ancient Ayurveda Acharya’s has given great emphasis on intake of ahara rasa as best source for nourishment that play prime role in growth and development of foetus during pregnancy. The ancient science of life not only has given priority to swasthavritta palana (daily and seasonal healthy regimen) but also given attention to ANC (antinatal care) for healthy progeny. The concept of shadbhava in Ayurveda represents the holistic framework integrating physical, psychological, spiritual aspects of foetal development. Classical references emphasize that harmonious interaction of these factors determines normal embryogenesis, while any imbalance may lead to congenital anamolies or impaired growth of foetus.

title: MEDICINAL EFFICACY AND PHARMACOLOGICAL PROFILE OF VIJAYSAR (PTEROCARPUS MARSUPIUM ROXB.), JARUL (LAGERSTROEMIA SPECIOSA LINN.), AND METHIKA (TRIGONELLA FOENUM-GRAECUM LINN.): A REVIEW ARTICLE
abstractText: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is the most common metabolic disorder characterized by chronic hyperglycaemia due to insulin resistance, impaired insulin secretion and progressive pancreatic β-cell dysfunction. Pharmacological treatments are effective, but the increasing prevalence of T2DM and the limitations of long-term therapy have led to an increased interest in complementary strategies such as medicinal plants. Some of the traditional plants with antidiabetic properties are Vijaysar (Pterocarpus marsupium Roxb.), Jarul or Banaba (Lagerstroemia speciosa (L.) Pers.) and Methika or Fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum L.). The biological activities of these have been ascribed to a wide variety of phytochemicals including epicatechin, pterostilbene, marsupin, corosolic acid, ellagitannins, galactomannan, 4-hydroxyisoleucine and steroidal saponins. Experimental studies indicate the possibility of these plants affecting glucose uptake, insulin secretion, insulin signaling, carbohydrate digestion, hepatic gluconeogenesis, oxidative stress and lipid metabolism. Also, human studies showed improvements in glycemic parameters, but the quality and quantity of evidence differs substantially between plants. Fenugreek has relatively better clinical data like randomized controlled trials and meta-analysis while Vijaysar and Jarul have lesser evidence. Here we review phytochemical composition, proposed mechanisms, experimental evidence, clinical studies, safety considerations and needs of future research of these three medicinal plants in T2DM. The successful integration of these botanicals into evidence-based management of diabetes will require standardization of plant preparations, rigorous randomized controlled trials and systematic evaluation of herb-drug interactions. title: The incorporation of interculturality in the training of health professionals: a systematic review
abstractText: ABSTRACT The training of health professionals has developed under the predominance of a biomedical rationality that tends to exclude traditional, indigenous, and community-based medical knowledge, despite the growing cultural diversity of Latin American societies. This systematic review aimed to analyze the available empirical evidence on the incorporation of interculturality into the curricula of university health science programs, in order to identify the main strengths, weaknesses, and training gaps reported in the literature, as well as the pedagogical and curricular strategies proposed to strengthen and implement it. Following the PRISMA 2020 statement and the eligibility criteria of the PICO model, a search was conducted in Scopus, Dialnet, Redalyc, LILACS, and SciELO, yielding a final sample of 27 studies reporting primary empirical data, published between 2020 and 2025. The results, organized through a narrative synthesis into four thematic categories, showed that interculturality has been incorporated predominantly in a declarative manner into institutional normative frameworks, but in most cases has not translated into an effective transformation of curricular content. Transversal and sustained training experiences were also identified, along with moderate levels of intercultural competence and sensitivity among students and faculty, and persistent structural barriers to care for indigenous, migrant, and Afro-descendant populations. The review concludes that a critical and effective curricular transformation toward interculturality requires strategies that go beyond the declarative incorporation of isolated content, moving instead toward cross-cutting curricular structures developed in direct dialogue with communities. RESUMEN La formación de profesionales de la salud se ha desarrollado bajo el predominio de una racionalidad biomédica que tiende a excluir los saberes médicos tradicionales, indígenas y comunitarios, pese a la creciente diversidad cultural de las sociedades latinoamericanas. El objetivo de esta revisión sistemática fue analizar la evidencia empírica disponible sobre la incorporación de la interculturalidad en el currículo de carreras universitarias del área de la salud, para identificar las principales fortalezas, debilidades y vacíos formativos reportados en la literatura, así como las estrategias pedagógicas y curriculares propuestas para su fortalecimiento. Siguiendo la declaración PRISMA 2020 y los criterios de elegibilidad del modelo PICO, se realizó una búsqueda en Scopus, Dialnet, Redalyc, LILACS y SciELO, que arrojó 27 estudios con datos empíricos primarios, publicados entre 2020 y 2025. Los resultados, organizados mediante síntesis narrativa en cuatro categorías temáticas, evidenciaron que la interculturalidad ha sido incorporada de manera predominantemente declarativa en los marcos normativos institucionales, sin traducirse, en la mayoría de los casos, en una transformación efectiva de los contenidos curriculares; asimismo, se identificaron experiencias formativas transversales y sostenidas en el tiempo, niveles moderados de competencia y sensibilidad intercultural en estudiantes y docentes, sin embargo, barreras estructurales persistentes en la atención a poblaciones indígenas, migrantes y afrodescendientes. Se concluye que la transformación curricular hacia una interculturalidad crítica y efectiva requiere estrategias que trasciendan la incorporación declarativa de contenidos puntuales, y se orienten hacia dispositivos curriculares transversales construidos en diálogo directo con las comunidades.

title: 'STIMULI-RESPONSIVE MUCOADHESIVE INTRANASAL IN SITU GELS FOR NOSE-TO-BRAIN DRUG DELIVERY: AN ADVANCED REVIEW ON BRAIN-TARGETING EFFICIENCY AND THERAPEUTIC HORIZONS
abstractText: comprehensive review systematically evaluates the development, physiological mechanisms, polymer chemistry, and brain-targeting performance of stimuli-responsive Mucoadhesive intranasal in situ gels designed for direct nose-to-brain (N2B) drug administration. Methods: A structured search strategy across PubMed and Scopus databases extracted SOTA peer-reviewed research (2019–2026) focusing on thermoresponsive, ion-activated, and pH-dependent polymer matrices combined with Nano carriers. Analytical screening emphasized absolute pharmacokinetic parameters including brain Area Under the Curve (AUC), Brain-Targeting Efficiency (BTE%), and Drug-Targeting Index (DTI). Results: The findings demonstrate that combining Nanoemulsion, solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs), or polymeric micelles within a smart Mucoadhesive hydrogel matrix extends the localized retention time within the olfactory region from less than 15 minutes to over 6 hours. This architectural shift significantly mitigates rapid mucociliary clearance (MCC) and bypasses the blood-brain barrier (BBB) via direct olfactory and trigeminal neuronal tracks. Conclusion: Stimuli-responsive nasal in situ gels offer a clinically viable, non-invasive platform for treating complex central nervous system (CNS) disorders, exhibiting up to an 8-fold increase in cerebral bioavailability compared to conventional oral therapeutics.

title: EFFECT OF KUPILU TAILA SHIROABHYANGA IN NIDRANASHA- A CLINICAL STUDY
abstractText: Nidranasha (insomnia) is one of the most commonly observed health problems in the present era, affecting both physical and psychological well-being. Sleep is a natural and essential physiological phenomenon that occupies nearly one-third of human life and plays a vital role in maintaining normal body functions, mental stability, and overall health. Proper sleep helps in maintaining physical strength, cognitive functions, emotional balance, and immunity. Therefore, understanding Nidranasha and its management through Ayurvedic principles is highly relevant in the current scenario for achieving holistic health and well-being. title: AN AYURVEDA THERAPEUTIC APPROACH TO THE MANAGEMENT OF SHITADA (GINGIVITIS): A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Background: Shitada is described among the diseases of Dantamoola and is characterized by clinical features such as gingival bleeding, altered gingival consistency, halitosis and other inflammatory changes. Its clinical presentation shows considerable correspondence with gingivitis, particularly when bleeding, edema, sponginess and redness of the gingiva are present. Case presentation: A 42 years old female Patient presented with bleeding from the gums during brushing, gingival swelling and foul smell from the mouth for 3 months. There was no history of systemic illness, previous surgery, tobacco, alcohol or other addiction. Oral examination revealed average oral hygiene, soft and spongy gingiva with a smooth, glazing-red surface, edema, grade 3 gingival hypertrophy, grade 3 halitosis and positive bleeding on probing. Intervention: The patient was advised Pratisarana with Kushtadi Churna mixed with honey twice daily and Triphala Churna 5 g HS with lukewarm water. The patient was reviewed at weekly intervals. Outcome: Subjective improvement was approximately 30% on day 7, 70% on day 14 and 95% on day 21. Gingival hypertrophy and halitosis progressively reduced from grade 3 to grade 2, then grade 1, and finally became absent. Bleeding on probing became negative by the third visit. At the fourth visit, the gingiva was clinically healthy, soft and pinkish, with no edema, halitosis or hypertrophy. Conclusion: The observed clinical improvement suggests that the selected Ayurveda oral-care regimen may have a beneficial role in the management of a clinical presentation corresponding to Shitada/gingivitis.

title: IN SILICO TOXICITY SCREENING: FROM CONVENTIONAL TO DIGITAL TOXICOLOGY
abstractText: Toxicity remains a major consideration in drug discovery because a compound must combine therapeutic activity with an acceptable safety profile. Conventional toxicity testing provides essential biological evidence but can be resource-intensive and may be difficult to apply to large chemical libraries at an early stage. In silico toxicity screening provides a complementary, data-driven approach for identifying potential safety liabilities before extensive experimental testing. This review summarises the transition from conventional toxicology to digital toxicology and discusses quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) modelling, read-across, molecular docking, toxicokinetic modelling, machine learning, deep learning and artificial intelligence (AI) approaches. Major toxicity endpoints, including cardiotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity, genotoxicity, carcinogenicity, reproductive and developmental toxicity, immunotoxicity and respiratory toxicity, are considered from a computational perspective. The article also examines how computational methods can support ADMET profiling, lead optimisation, candidate prioritisation and early toxicity-based deprioritisation. Although digital methods can improve speed, scalability and consistency, their reliability depends on data quality, model validation, applicability domain, interpretability and experimental confirmation. Future toxicology is expected to increasingly integrate AI, multi-omics, human-relevant in vitro systems, organ-on-chip models and New Approach Methodologies (NAMs). Overall, computational toxicity assessment is best viewed as a complementary component of an integrated safety strategy rather than a replacement for experimental toxicology.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF CLOTRIMAZOLE-LOADED NANOEMULGEL FOR ENHANCED TOPICAL ANTIFUNGAL DELIVERY
abstractText: Background: Clotrimazole is a widely used topical imidazole antifungal; however, its physicochemical properties and limited skin penetration can restrict effective drug delivery from conventional topical formulations. Nanoemulgel systems offer a promising approach by combining the nanoscale characteristics of nanoemulsions with the prolonged residence and improved application properties of a gel base. Objective: The present study aimed to develop and optimize a clotrimazole-loaded nanoemulgel for enhanced topical drug delivery, skin permeation, skin retention, and antifungal activity. Methods: Preformulation studies of clotrimazole included organoleptic characterization, solubility, melting point, and partition coefficient determination. Based on solubility screening, oleic acid, Tween 80, and Transcutol P were selected as the oil, surfactant, and co-surfactant, respectively. Pseudo-ternary phase diagrams were constructed, and six nanoemulsion formulations (F1–F6) were prepared using high-speed homogenization followed by ultrasonication. The optimized nanoemulsion was incorporated into Carbopol 934 gel to prepare four nanoemulgel formulations (NG1–NG4). Formulations were evaluated for physicochemical characteristics, in-vitro drug diffusion and release kinetics. The optimized nanoemulgel was further assessed for ex-vivo skin permeation and retention and antifungal activity against Candida albicans and Aspergillus niger. Results: Clotrimazole exhibited maximum solubility in oleic acid (82.45 ± 1.24 mg/mL), Tween 80 (95.64 ± 1.42 mg/mL), and Transcutol P (108.52 ± 1.63 mg/mL). Formulation F5 showed the smallest droplet size (98.4 ± 1.82 nm) and lowest polydispersity index (0.164 ± 0.005), and was selected as the optimized nanoemulsion. Among the nanoemulgels, NG4 demonstrated superior performance, with 96.82 ± 0.58% drug diffusion at 12 h. Drug-release analysis showed the best fit with the Higuchi model (R² = 0.989), while the Korsmeyer–Peppas diffusion exponent (n = 0.684) indicated non-Fickian release. Compared with conventional clotrimazole gel, NG4 exhibited higher 12-h drug permeation (624.48 ± 1.58 vs. 436.26 ± 1.32 µg/cm²), flux (52.84 ± 1.06 vs. 36.42 ± 1.12 µg/cm²/h), and skin retention (246.82 ± 1.94 vs. 128.46 ± 2.08 µg/cm²). NG4 also produced larger zones of inhibition against C. albicans (31.8 ± 0.72 mm) and A. niger (28.4 ± 0.68 mm) than the conventional gel. Conclusion: The optimized clotrimazole-loaded nanoemulgel demonstrated favorable physicochemical characteristics, controlled drug release, enhanced skin permeation and retention, and improved antifungal activity compared with the conventional formulation. The developed nanoemulgel therefore represents a promising topical delivery system for improving the therapeutic performance of clotrimazole.

title: PHARMACEUTICO-ANALYTICAL STUDY OF CLASSICAL SHANKHA BHASMA COMPARING WITH DIFFERENT MARKET SAMPLES BY RAMAN SPECTROSCOPY
abstractText: Shankha Bhasma is an important Ayurvedic mineral preparation derived from Shankha and is traditionally prepared through specific pharmaceutical procedures including Shodhana, Bhavana and Marana. Proper pharmaceutical processing is essential for achieving the desired physicochemical characteristics and therapeutic suitability of the final product. With increasing availability of commercially marketed Bhasma preparations, scientific analytical methods are necessary to assess their quality and to identify similarities or differences between traditionally prepared and marketed samples. Aim: To prepare Classical Shankha Bhasma according to classical Ayurvedic references and to compare the prepared Bhasma with different marketed samples using pharmaceutical and analytical parameters, with special emphasis on Raman spectroscopy. Materials and Methods: Shankha was subjected to classical Shodhana followed by Marana using appropriate Bhavana Dravya and repeated incineration procedures as described in classical Rasashastra texts. The prepared Classical Shankha Bhasma was evaluated using classical Bhasma Pariksha and physicochemical parameters. Six marketed samples were collected and subjected to comparative analysis. Analytical evaluation included pH, loss on drying, total ash, acid-insoluble ash, water-soluble ash, particle-size-related observations, SEM–EDX and Raman spectroscopic analysis. Results: The prepared and marketed samples showed variation in physicochemical and analytical characteristics. The pH values of the evaluated marketed samples ranged from 8 to 14. Total ash values ranged from 94.06% to 100%, while acid-insoluble ash values ranged from 97.2% to 99.7%. Water-soluble ash showed greater variation, ranging from 64.16% to 100%. Loss on drying ranged from 0.3% to 1.2%. SEM–EDX demonstrated differences in elemental composition and surface morphology among the samples. Raman spectroscopy provided characteristic spectral information useful for comparative identification and differentiation of the samples. Conclusion: The study demonstrates the importance of integrating classical Ayurvedic pharmaceutical principles with modern analytical techniques for the standardization of Shankha Bhasma. Raman spectroscopy, together with physicochemical and microscopic techniques, may serve as a useful rapid and non-destructive analytical tool for comparative evaluation and quality assessment of Shankha Bhasma.

title: EARLY MENARCHE: AN EMERGING REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH CHALLENGE CURRENT EVIDENCE AND AYURVEDIC PERSPECTIVES
abstractText: Early menarche is the onset of the first menstrual period at an unusually young age. Menarche before 10 years is generally considered early; however, menstruation at this age requires clinical assessment because it may indicate rapidly progressive puberty or an underlying endocrine disorder. Early menarche is influenced by genetic predisposition, childhood adiposity, nutritional status, neuroendocrine maturation, psychosocial adversity and possible exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals. Its clinical relevance extends beyond the timing of the first period and includes psychosocial distress, earlier epiphyseal maturation, and associations with later metabolic and reproductive health outcomes. This descriptive review summarises normal pubertal physiology, causes and consequences of early menarche, clinical assessment and management, and preventive concepts described in Ayurveda.

title: ABHRAKA BHASMA AND THE NEURONAL EPIGENOME: A HYPOTHETICAL FRAMEWORK LINKING NANOSTRUCTURE, MECHANOTRANSDUCTION, AND LONG-TERM POTENTIATION
abstractText: Background: Abhraka Bhasma is a traditionally processed mineral preparation of Rasashastra with described Rasayana applications and associations with Majja Dhatu and cognitive functions. Contemporary physicochemical investigations have demonstrated that pharmaceutical processing can produce substantial changes in the mineral's elemental composition, crystallinity, particle characteristics, and morphology. These findings raise the possibility that the biological effects of Abhraka Bhasma may involve mechanisms beyond conventional chemical interactions. Mechanobiology provides a potential framework for investigating how the physicochemical characteristics of mineral-derived materials may interact with cellular mechanosensing, cytoskeletal signaling, nuclear regulation, and neuronal plasticity. Aim and Objectives: The aim of this review is to develop a hypothesis-driven framework linking the physicochemical characteristics of Abhraka Bhasma with mechanotransduction, epigenetic regulation, and neuronal synaptic plasticity, particularly long-term potentiation (LTP). The objectives are to review the Ayurvedic and pharmaceutical basis of Abhraka Bhasma; evaluate its contemporary physicochemical and nanoscale characteristics; examine evidence relating extracellular mechanics and mechanotransduction to neuronal function; explore the relationship between mechanical signaling, chromatin regulation, and neuronal plasticity; and identify experimentally testable pathways connecting Abhraka-derived material properties with neuronal mechanotransduction and LTP. Materials And Methods: A structured narrative literature review was conducted using databases including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, AYUSH Research Portal, and DHARA Online, along with relevant classical Ayurvedic literature. Literature concerning Abhraka Bhasma and Rasashastra, mineral nanomaterials, mechanobiology, mechanotransduction, neuroepigenetics, mechanical memory, neuronal plasticity, and LTP was identified and critically synthesized. Evidence from these domains was integrated to develop a conceptual Abhraka–neuronal epigenome framework. No primary experimental investigation was performed. Observation And Results: The reviewed literature indicates that Abhraka Bhasma is a complex processed mineral material whose physicochemical characteristics can vary according to pharmaceutical preparation and analytical methodology. Independent evidence from mechanobiology demonstrates that extracellular mechanical conditions can influence neuronal development, synaptic organization, and network activity through mechanosensing systems involving integrin-associated structures, mechanically activated ion channels, cytoskeletal signaling, and YAP/TAZ-mediated mechanotransduction. Mechanical signaling can also influence nuclear organization, chromatin regulation, and transcriptional programs, while mechanical memory has been demonstrated predominantly in non-neuronal cellular systems. In neuronal plasticity, activity-dependent calcium signaling, gene transcription, and structural synaptic modifications contribute to persistent changes associated with LTP. Integration of these findings provides a hypothetical mechanistic framework in which the physicochemical characteristics of appropriately prepared Abhraka Bhasma could potentially interact with neuronal or glial cell–material interfaces and influence mechanotransductive and epigenetic pathways relevant to synaptic plasticity. However, direct evidence demonstrating CNS delivery, neuronal mechanotransduction, epigenetic modification, or LTP induction by Abhraka Bhasma is currently lacking. Conclusion: The available evidence supports consideration of Abhraka Bhasma as a potential subject for interdisciplinary investigation at the interface of Rasashastra, materials science, mechanobiology, and neuroepigenetics. The proposed Abhraka–neuronal epigenome framework provides a testable hypothesis rather than an established mechanism, linking mineral-derived physicochemical characteristics with possible mechanotransduction, chromatin regulation, and neuronal plasticity. Experimental studies addressing material characterization, biological availability, cell–material interactions, mechanosensitive signaling, epigenetic changes, neuronal network activity, and LTP are required to evaluate this proposed relationship.

title: NIDRA AND MANAS BHAVA: A CORRELATIVE REVIEW OF RAJAS AND TAMAS GUNA WITH MODERN SLEEP PHYSIOLOGY
abstractText: Background: Nidra (sleep) is an essential physiological process that contributes to physical restoration, cognitive functioning, emotional regulation, and overall well-being. Ayurveda recognises Nidra as one of the three Upastambha, along with Ahara and Brahmacharya. The Ayurvedic understanding of sleep incorporates the functioning of Manas and the influence of the three Gunas—Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. Aim: To critically review the relationship between Nidra and Manas Bhava, with particular emphasis on Rajas and Tamas Guna, and to explore their conceptual correlation with contemporary sleep physiology. Materials and Methods: A narrative review was undertaken using classical Ayurvedic literature, including Charaka Samhita and Sushruta Samhita, along with published scientific literature concerning sleep regulation, psychological stress, cognitive arousal, and emotional functioning. Relevant concepts were examined to identify areas of conceptual convergence and differences between traditional Ayurvedic explanations and modern physiological knowledge. Review: Ayurvedic literature describes sleep in relation to the functional state of Manas, Indriyas, and the predominance of Tamas. Rajas, associated with activity, stimulation, and mental agitation, provides a conceptual framework for discussing persistent mental activity that may interfere with sleep. Modern research identifies psychological stress, repetitive negative thinking, and cognitive hyperarousal as factors associated with sleep disturbances. Sleep itself also influences memory, attention, mood, and emotional regulation. These findings support an interdisciplinary examination of the relationship between mental states and sleep, although the Ayurvedic Gunas cannot be considered direct equivalents of modern neurophysiological mechanisms. Conclusion: Nidra and Manas Bhava represent interconnected dimensions of health in Ayurveda. The concepts of Rajas and Tamas offer a traditional framework for examining mental activity and sleep, while contemporary sleep science provides complementary explanations of sleep–wake regulation. Further empirical research using validated psychological and sleep-assessment tools is required to establish measurable associations between Ayurvedic constructs and modern clinical parameters.

title: AN REVIEW ARTICLE ON EFFECT OF DIET AND LIFESTYLE MODIFICATIONS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF GRAHANI ROG
abstractText: Grahani Roga is a well-established functional gastrointestinal disorder in Ayurvedic medicine, characterised by impairment of the intestinal seat of digestion and absorption, designated Grahani. The condition bears significant clinical overlap with what contemporary gastroenterology describes as Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). Classical treatises identify disturbed Agni (digestive fire) as the central pathological event, precipitated primarily by faulty dietary practices, irregular lifestyle, and psychosocial stress. To synthesise classical Ayurvedic textual evidence and contemporary scientific literature in elucidating the role of diet and lifestyle in the aetiopathogenesis and management of Grahani Roga. A narrative review was conducted drawing from primary Ayurvedic classical texts — Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya, Madhava Nidana, Bhavaprakasha, Chakradatta, and Yoga Ratnakara — and from peer-reviewed modern gastroenterological literature retrieved through PubMed, Scopus, and AYUSH-affiliated databases. Pathya Ahara (wholesome diet), Dinacharya (regulated daily regimen), Sansarjana Krama (graduated dietary rehabilitation), and psychosomatic interventions collectively constitute the foundation of Grahani Roga management, corroborated by contemporary evidence on gut-brain axis modulation and microbiota regulation.

title: PHARMACEUTICAL INDUSTRY PARTNERSHIPS AND PRESCRIBING PRACTICES IN MALI: A MIXED-METHODS STUDY OF INFLUENCE ON CLINICAL DECISIONS AND CARE PROTOCOLS
abstractText: Objectives: To assess how pharmaceutical industry partnerships influence prescribing practices and the development of clinical care protocols in Mali, where out-of-pocket health expenditures reach nearly 40% of total health spending. Methods: We conducted a sequential mixed-methods study from January to December 2026 in Commune III of Bamako. The quantitative phase surveyed 331 health professionals, 90 patients, and 94 pharmaceutical industry representatives using electronic questionnaires. The qualitative phase involved semi-structured interviews with protocol drafters and health decisionmakers. We used descriptive statistics, Spearman correlations, and multivariate regressions to analyze associations between industry exposure and prescribing outcomes. Results: Partnerships were intense and nearly universal. All professionals (100%) reported receiving promotional gifts, 87.3% received free samples, and 52.9% received offered meals. Medical representatives averaged 17.4 professional contacts per day. Brand-name prescribing dominated: professionals prescribed brand-name specialties in 73.2% of prescriptions on average, and 68.7% did so in 7 or more of every 10 prescriptions (Figure 1). We found no significant correlation between industry exposure score and brand-name prescribing (r = 0.13; P = .535). Being a physician was the only factor significantly associated with increased brand-name prescribing (β = 1.57; P < .001; Table 1). All patients (100%) were aware of medical representatives' influence, and 42.2% had forgone care because of cost (Table 2). One-third of protocol drafters considered industry participation in guideline development unacceptable. Conclusions: Pharmaceutical partnerships in Mali are intense and coexist with high rates of brand-name prescribing an indicator of irrational prescribing. Although exposure to industry benefits was not directly correlated with brand-name prescribing in this study, the normalization of these practices and their financial impact on patients demand urgent, context-adapted regulation.

title: CLINICAL OUTCOMES OF ANULOMANA THERAPY IN GRADE I INTERNAL HEMORRHOIDS: A CASE SERIES
abstractText: Background: Grade I internal hemorrhoids present with bleeding per rectum without prolapse, and constipation (Vibandha) is a key aggravating factor. In Arsha, Anulomana is the first step of Bheshaja Chikitsa. This case series aimed to document bowel regularity and symptom outcomes after Anulomana therapy in Grade I internal Hemorrhoids. Materials and Methods: Three patients (38-year-old male, 32-year-old female, 45-year-old male) with proctoscopically confirmed Grade I internal Hemorrhoids and constipation were treated at the Shalya Tantra OPD and reported as per CARE guidelines. They received Avipattikara Churna, Swadishta Virechana Churna and Triphala Churna respectively, 5 g at bedtime with lukewarm water for 30 days, with Pathyahara. The primary outcome was bowel regularity (Bristol Stool Form Scale, frequency, straining, complete evacuation). Secondary outcomes were Hemorrhoid Severity Score (HSS) and bleeding, assessed at Day 0, 15 and 30. Results: All three patients achieved regular bowel habit by Day 30, shifting from hard stools (Bristol Type 1-2) with straining. Bleeding was controlled in all. HSS fell from 7, 6 and 5 at baseline to 1, 1 and 0 respectively. No adverse events occurred. Conclusion: Anulomana therapy with Pathyahara for 30 days was associated with regular bowel habit, cessation of bleeding and reduced symptom scores in Grade I internal hemorrhoids, supporting correction of Vibandha and Apana Vata as first-line care. Larger controlled studies with recurrence follow-up are warranted.

title: EFFICACY OF KSHEERBALA TAIL YOGBASTI AND VRUDHDARUK GHRITA NASYA IN INFERTILITY
abstractText: Infertility is defined as failure to conceive though having regular unprotected coitus for more than a year.[1] The male is directly responsible in about 30-40%, the female in about 40-50% and both are responsible in about 10% cases. The remaining 10% is unexplained.[2] Infertility primarily refers to the biological inability of a person to contribute to conception. title: REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR THE APPROVAL OF NANOPARTICLES AS PER CDSCO IN INDIA COMPARISON WITH SINGAPORE
abstractText: This study examines the regulatory requirements for nanoparticles medications in Singapore and India are compared in this abstract. It draws attention to the frameworks set up by Singapore's Health Sciences Authority (HSA) and India's Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO). The procedures for clinical studies, approval schedules, and post-marketing surveillance are among the main distinctions. Singapore places a strong emphasis on strict safety and efficacy criteria, whereas India stresses a quicker clearance process to address pressing healthcare needs. The investigation highlights how various regulatory methods affect patient access, innovation, and medicine supply in both nations. Nanotechnology has emerged as a transformative field with applications spanning medicine, environmental science, and materials engineering. This thesis presents a comparative analysis of nanoparticle synthesis, characterization, and application trends in India and Singapore, focusing on silver nanoparticles (AgNanoparticles) and metal oxide nanoparticles. The study evaluates methodologies such as green synthesis using plant extracts—widely adopted in India for its eco-friendly and cost-effective nature.

title: A CLINICAL STUDY TO EVALUATE THE EFFECT OF VYAGHRI TAILA NASYA IN THE MANAGEMENT OF DUSHTA PRATISHYAYA W.S.R. TO CHRONIC SINUSITIS
abstractText: Background: Dushta Pratishyaya is described in Ayurvedic classics as a chronic and complicated form of Pratishyaya, which may be clinically correlated with Chronic Sinusitis. Chronic Sinusitis is characterized by persistent inflammation of the nose and paranasal sinuses, presenting with nasal obstruction, nasal discharge, sneezing, headache, post-nasal discharge and impaired sense of smell. Nasya Karma is an important therapeutic procedure for Urdhvajatrugata Vyadhi. Aim and Objectives: To evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of Vyaghri Taila Nasya in the management of Dushta Pratishyaya w.s.r. to Chronic Sinusitis. Materials and Methods: A single-arm clinical study was conducted on 10 patients diagnosed with Dushta Pratishyaya w.s.r. to Chronic Sinusitis according to Ayurvedic and contemporary diagnostic criteria. Patients above 12 years of either gender were selected from the Department of Shalakya Tantra, R.G.G.P.G. Ayurvedic College and Hospital, Paprola, Kangra, H.P. Vyaghri Taila Nasya was administered for 30 days as per the prescribed protocol. Clinical assessment was performed before and after treatment, with follow-up on the 15th and 30th days. Observations and Results: Improvement was observed in clinical features including nasal obstruction, nasal discharge, sneezing, headache and post-nasal discharge, with reduction in associated sinonasal symptoms. No significant adverse effects were observed. Conclusion: Vyaghri Taila Nasya showed beneficial effects in the management of Dushta Pratishyaya. Larger controlled clinical studies are required to establish its efficacy conclusively.

title: AYURVEDIC MANAGEMENT OF AVATU GRANTHI ROGA (HYPOTHYROIDISM)- A CASE STUDY
abstractText: Hypothyroidism is a common endocrine disorder characterized by inadequate production of thyroid hormones, resulting in metabolic disturbances and a reduction in the basal metabolic rate. In Ayurveda, diseases of the thyroid gland can be correlated with Avatu Granthi Roga. Ayurveda emphasizes identification and management of the underlying causative factors and considers the involvement of Kapha-Vata Dosha, Rasavaha Srotas, Medovaha Srotas, and Agnimandya in the manifestation of the condition. A 35-year-old female patient presented with Sthaulya (weight gain), Daurbalya (weakness), Twak Rukshata (dry skin), Kesha Patana (hair loss), Akshikut shotha (periorbital puffiness), mood swings, impaired memory, emotional distress, Tandra (drowsiness), Shirshool (headache), Amlapitta (hyperacidity), and elevated thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) and normal T3 and T4 levels for approximately four years. She had been receiving conventional medical treatment but reported inadequate relief in her symptoms. An Ayurvedic treatment protocol consisting of a group of herbo-mineral preparations was administered for four months and experienced relief in her symptoms and decrease in TSH level. Her allopathy medicines completely stopped.

title: AYURVEDIC MANAGEMENT OF ANOVULATORY INFERTILITY ASSOCIATED WITH POLYCYSTIC OVARY SYNDROME (PCOS): A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a common cause of ovulatory dysfunction and female infertility. In Ayurveda, infertility is described as Vandhyatva, and menstrual and ovulatory disturbances may be interpreted in terms of Artava Dushti and Artavavaha Srotodushti. A 26-year-old woman presented with PCOS-associated anovulatory infertility, irregular menstrual cycles, and a history of infertility treatment without conception. Investigations revealed bilateral polycystic ovarian morphology and anovulatory cycles. The patient received an individualized Ayurvedic treatment protocol comprising Virechana Karma, Basti Chikitsa, including Uttara Basti, oral medications, and supportive procedures. The treatment approach was based on the Ayurvedic principles of Dosha Shamana, Agni Deepana, and management of Artava Dushti. Following the treatment course, the patient conceived and subsequently delivered a healthy male infant weighing 3.5 kg. This case describes a favorable reproductive outcome following an individualized Ayurvedic treatment protocol in a woman with PCOS-associated anovulatory infertility. However, as this is a single case involving multiple interventions, a causal relationship between the treatment and conception cannot be established, and the contribution of individual therapies cannot be determined. Further systematic clinical studies are required to evaluate the efficacy and safety of this approach.

title: REFINING THE ART OF VISION: YOGARATNAKARA'S INSIGHTS INTO NETRA ROGA CHIKITSA
abstractText: The current article presents a comprehensive consolidated knowledge regarding the management of different netra roga and also in maintaining the Netra swastya as elaborated in Ayurvedic classic - Yogaratnakara. The text Yogaratnakara is known for its practical, clinically oriented approach, compiles extensive yogas and yogya chikitsa for diverse netra rogas. This makes it a significant reference for a Shalaki in the perspective as a Drushti visharada. This article brings together the valuable descriptions from Yogaratnakara, highlighting its pratyeka yogas, different karmas and upakarmas, diseased based chikitsa. A wide range of classical preparations such as kwatha (decoctions), churna (powders), ghrita (ghee), taila (oil) and anjana yogas (collyrium)—are systematically presented along with their method of preparations, indications, contraindications across diverse netra rogas. The important procedures including seka (irrigation), ashchyotana (eye drops), tarpana (nourishing eye therapy using ghee), putapaka (a procedure like tarpana done with extracted juice), jalouka (leech therapy), lekhana (scrapping) and bhedana (incision) are explained with its expected clinical outcome. Even the Atyayika chikitsa (emergency management) like siravyadha (venesection), upanaha (warm poultice) and specialized practices including pindika (application of paste on the entire eyes using a cloth), bidalaka (application of paste on eye excluding eye lashes) are explained with its practical relevance. Internal medications such as Triphala kaṣhaya, Saptamrita loha, Madhukadi loha, Shuddha guggulu, Patoladi ghrita, Vasakadi kwatha are described with their systemic and local benefits. Pathyas (wholesome), lifestyle guidelines and behavioural considerations affecting ocular health—such as nidra (sleep), atapa sevana (exposure to sunlight), ratri-jagarana (awakening at night) and dietary choices—are summarized to present the integrative nature of Ayurvedic ophthalmology. Overall, this article establishes Yogaratnakara as a crucial, clinically rich source for understanding and treating netra rogas, offering a unified reference for contemporary Ayurvedic practice.

title: POTATO CHIPS INDUCED HISTOLOGICAL CHANGES IN THE LIVER OF WISTAR ALBINO RATS AND ITS MANAGEMENT WITH BHRINGARAJA SWARASA
abstractText: Background: The liver is the principal organ of metabolism, detoxification and biotransformation, and is highly vulnerable to dietary and oxidative insults. Rising consumption of processed, deep-fried potato chips, rich in oxidised fats, excess salt and acrylamide formed during frying, has been linked to hepatocellular injury. Many Rasayana drugs have hepatoprotective activity, one among them is Bhringaraja (Eclipta alba). Objective: To evaluate potato chips induced hepatotoxicity, with liver function test and liver histopathology and to assess the curative efficacy of Bhringaraja Swarasa in Wistar albino rats. Methods: Eighteen adult Wistar albino rats (weighing around 200–250 gm) were allotted to three groups of six each, i.e, Group I (control), Group II (disease group) and Group III (curative group). Liver function tests (LFTs) and liver histopathological test were performed at the end of each phase. Results: Group II showed marked elevation of Aspartate amino Transferase (AST), Alanine amino Transferase (ALT) and Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP), compared with control (p < 0.001), with histopathology showing hepatocyte ballooning, cytoplasmic vacuolation, sinusoidal congestion and inflammatory infiltration. Group III showed significant biochemical recovery and near-restoration of normal hepatic lobular architecture. Conclusion: Chronic potato chips consumption produces measurable structural and biochemical hepatotoxicity in rats and Bhringaraja Swarasa demonstrates significant hepatoprotective and hepato-regenerative activity.

title: PREOPERATIVE TOPICAL NONSTEROIDAL ANTI-INFLAMMATORY DRUGS IN THE PREVENTION OF INTRAOPERATIVE FLOPPY IRIS SYNDROME: A REVIEW ARTICLE
abstractText: Intraoperative floppy iris syndrome is a form of small pupil in which the iris becomes flaccid and billows with irrigation currents, prolapses toward the incisions, and constricts progressively during cataract surgery. It is most strongly associated with tamsulosin, an alpha-1A adrenoceptor antagonist, and it prolongs surgery and raises the risk of intraoperative complications. Standard dilating drops often fail in affected eyes because the iris dilator muscle is pharmacologically impaired. However, part of the pupil constriction seen during surgery is driven by prostaglandins released in response to surgical trauma. Topical nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs inhibit cyclooxygenase, reduce prostaglandin synthesis, and are used routinely before cataract surgery to maintain mydriasis. This review summarizes the pathophysiology of intraoperative floppy iris syndrome, the pharmacology of the available topical agents (flurbiprofen, ketorolac, diclofenac, bromfenac, and nepafenac), and the clinical evidence for their use. Randomised and comparative studies in cataract surgery show that ketorolac, nepafenac, and bromfenac help to maintain pupil diameter, and head-to-head comparisons favor ketorolac and nepafenac over flurbiprofen. Direct evidence in patients at risk of the syndrome comes mainly from intracameral phenylephrine-ketorolac, which reduced iris prolapse and billowing in men taking tamsulosin. No high-quality trial has tested preoperative topical nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs alone against placebo for preventing the syndrome itself. These drugs are best regarded as a low-risk adjunct within a multimodal strategy that also uses atropine, intracameral epinephrine, viscoelastic agents, and mechanical pupil expansion when needed.

title: PHARMACEUTICAL AND ANALYTICAL STUDY OF JATI GHRITA
abstractText: Background: Ghrita is thought to be the best of the different Snehakalpanas.[1] It has a special ability to absorb extra pharmacological qualities from integrated medications while maintaining its own intrinsic qualities. Additionally, the body accepts Ghrita well, increasing its therapeutic efficiency without sacrificing its original properties. Ashtang sangraha mentions Jati ghrita as one of the remedies for Visha, Kushta, and other conditions. Jati patra kwath, Jati patra kalka, and cow's ghee are the ingredients of Jati ghrita. Aim: To carry out the pharmaceutical preparation of Jati Ghrita and to analyze the prepared Jati Ghrita. Materials and Methods: Jati Ghrita is a unique formulation which comes under snehakalpana prepared by the general method of sneha preparation. It is indicated in visha, mukhpak, kushta. Results: The pharmaceutical study showed that there were no pharmaceutical errors in the preparation of Jati Ghrita. The analytical parameters helped establish preliminary standards for Jati Ghrita according to the testing protocols. The GC-MS technique aided in identifying and documenting the active components present in the sample.

title: A STUDY TO ASSESS THE AWARENESS & UTILIZATION OF MATERNITY BENEFIT SCHEMES AMONG MOTHERS HAVING 0-5 YEARS AGED CHILDREN IN A SELECTED PRIMARY HEALTH CENTRE, BANGALORE
abstractText: Background of the study: The Maternity Benefit Scheme is a social welfare program designed to support the health and well-being of expectant and new mothers. It aims to ensure that women can maintain their physical and mental health during pregnancy and the postpartum period while securing financial stability. Maternity well-being under this scheme is not limited to medical care but also includes nutritional support, rest, and protection from work-related stress or hazards. This holistic approach promotes healthier mothers, reduces maternal and infant morbidity, and contributes to the overall development of families. Method of the study: The research design of the present study was an overall plan for obtaining answer to the research questions or testing the research hypothesis. In the present study descriptive co-relational research design was adopted. The subjects selected for the study were mothers having children aged 0 to 5 years, who were residing at konanakunte PHC, Banglore. Sample of the study consisted of 60 mothers and were selected by convenient sampling method. The tool used for collection of data is a structured questionnaire. Result: There was a positive co-relation between level of awareness and level of utilization, therefore H1 hypothesis is accepted and also there was a significant association between level of awareness and a demographic variable, therefore H2 hypothesis is accepted. Interpretation: From the above findings the null hypothesis is rejected and research hypothesis is completely accepted with regards to selected background variables. Conclusion: Thus from the above study, the investigators has proved that there is a significant relationship between awareness and utilization, hence proving the H1 hypothesis along with show casting the association between level of awareness with the selected demographic data, therefore proving the H2 hypothesis.

title: ETHNO PHARMACOLOGY AND THE SCIENTIFIC INTEGRATION OF TRADITIONAL MEDICINE: ADVANCING HOLISTIC AND EVIDENCE-BASED HEALTHCARE
abstractText: Traditional medicine systems continue to serve as primary healthcare resources for a substantial proportion of the global population, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where access to modern medical infrastructure remains limited. Ethnopharmacology has emerged as a critical interdisciplinary field that systematically bridges indigenous knowledge systems with contemporary biomedical science, enabling scientific validation, standardization, and integration of traditional therapeutic practices. This comprehensive review examines the evolving role of ethnopharmacology in advancing holistic treatment paradigms through methodological innovations such as network pharmacology, systems biology, metabolomics, artificial intelligence, and multi-omics technologies. The paper critically analyzes multimodal therapeutic strategies, constitutional typing frameworks, and mind–body integration approaches embedded within traditional medicine systems. Furthermore, it evaluates current challenges related to clinical validation, quality control, regulatory harmonization, safety assessment, and ethical issues including intellectual property rights and equitable benefit-sharing. Emerging evidence suggests that traditional medicine offers promising complementary strategies for managing complex chronic and multifactorial diseases; however, rigorous interdisciplinary research, robust clinical methodologies, and culturally sensitive policy frameworks are essential for its sustainable integration into global healthcare systems. Strengthening collaborations between traditional knowledge holders and scientific communities will be pivotal in developing equitable, evidence-based, and patient-centered holistic healthcare models.

title: INTEGRATED REVIEW OF ANTIFUNGAL RESISTANCE: MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS, CLINICAL CHALLENGES AND THERAPEUTICS INTERVENTION
abstractText: Deeply invasive fungal infections are emerging as an increasingly substantial worldwide healthcare challenge, especially for medically compromised and individuals with weakened immune systems. The aforementioned infectious conditions are challenging to address because clinical diagnosis is often prolonged and mycotic organisms swiftly acquire resistance against commonly used drug classes such as azoles, polyenes, and echinocandins. In the present review, we explore the molecular and cellular mechanisms responsible for antifungal resistance, incorporating modifications at drug target sites, overexpression of targets, upregulation of stress‑response pathways like Hsp90 and calcineurin, genomic flexibility, and drug efflux through transporters such as ABC and MFS families. We also discuss diagnostic strategies, from traditional methods to modern molecular and biomarker‑based assays. Special emphasis is devoted to WHO‑listed highest-priority pathogens such as Candida auris, and the therapeutic innovations currently being investigated to combat them. These involve next‑generation antifungals (fosmanogepix, ibrexafungerp, rezafungin), naturally derived compounds, combination therapies, biologics, and nanotechnology‑based delivery systems. Ultimately, strengthening patient outcomes worldwide will require integrating sophisticated diagnostic approaches with these emerging treatment to counteract existing clinical challenges.

title: AN OBSERVATIONAL STUDY ON RELATION BETWEEN SHAREERA PRAKRITI AND AMLAPITTA
abstractText: Prakriti is one of the fundamental concepts of Ayurveda and represents the unique constitutional makeup of an individual, determined at the time of conception by the relative predominance of Dosha.[1] It is considered a stable, lifelong attribute that influences the physical, physiological, psychological, and behavioural characteristics of an individual, along with disease susceptibility, prognosis, and response to treatment. Among the various methods of Rogi Pareeksha described in Ayurvedic classics, Prakriti Pareeksha occupies a central position as it provides the basis for individualized assessment and personalized healthcare. Ayurvedic classics describe that individuals with predominant Dosha are more susceptible to disorders related to the same Dosha when exposed to appropriate Nidana[2], emphasizing the role of constitutional predisposition in the manifestation of disease.

title: FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF CUBOSOMES FOR ENHANCED DELIVERY OF APIGENIN
abstractText: The present study focused on the formulation and evaluation of Apigenin-loaded cubosomes for enhanced drug delivery. Pre-formulation studies confirmed the suitability of Apigenin, which showed poor aqueous solubility, a melting point of 346°C, pH 6.4, and λmax at 327 nm. The formulation was optimized using a Box–Behnken Design (BBD) under Quality by Design (QbD) principles, with Glyceryl Monooleate (GMO), Poloxamer 407, and stirring time selected as critical formulation variables. The optimized formulation showed a particle size of 196.32 nm, zeta potential of −23.4 mV, and entrapment efficiency of 95.578%. SEM analysis revealed nearly spherical nanoparticles with a rough surface morphology. The optimized cubosomes exhibited sustained drug release, reaching 92.56% over 12 h. Drug release kinetics showed the best fit with the Zero-order model (R² = 0.951), indicating controlled drug release. Overall, the findings demonstrate that Apigenin-loaded cubosomes can provide a suitable lipid-based nanocarrier for improving the delivery of poorly water-soluble Apigenin.
